We’ve been doing routine root touch-ups every 5-6 weeks using professional bond building additives (olaplex or ultim8 bond) to protect her hair from any damage or dryness. Blonde is not a color to be messed with. You need to do research on your water source, invest in professional products, and most importantly.. your STYLIST. Good hair isn’t cheap, and cheap hair isn’t good. It’s our job to protect your hair at all costs. We don’t advise you drop pennies on product or pre-book tones/conditioning treatments in-between services because we want your money. We just want you to have healthy hair. Healthy hair holds color properly, holds curl, and continues to hold natural protein. Damaged hair from the use of drugstore products will create a build up on the outer layer preventing it from taking color well, staying healthy, and holding any style forms. Before you have the mindset that it’s your stylists fault, remember that we are here to help you and we are your friend! We will always be available to help guide you to the proper products for your specific hair needs. Please stop spending $100+ on your hair then purchasing products on amazon. This look was inspired by @dressyourface on a model. 
During the end of 2014 , while I was pursuing my internship program in medicine, I decided to start Makeup( as a temporary means of earning money for my tuition fees) 
I knew what I wanted, but didn’t really know how to start. 
Although I wasn’t quite great in the past, I still managed to do a couple of looks for my friends on their wedding day & also worked for few brands for their campaigns.

I have always been good with winged liners, it was just effortless for me to do it, & that’s pretty much about it. 
Before I could take clients, I kept thinking for months (I’m very indecisive & a Perfectionist) if I should  take a Makeup course.

Later, I decided to volunteer as a model for a Makeup academy. Apparently, it was the last day of the student & she was still quite clumsy with the Application. 
When I saw my self in the mirror! That was the moment when I decided, I don’t have to spend money on a training course. Would rather invest in Makeup.

I was even ready to pay a MUA , watching her do a real bride for ONCE so, I could have an idea, but that never happened.

Fast forward .. Couldn’t watch YT videos, though I did skim through a few, coz that’s too much process. 
So, I watched a handful of @gossmakeupartist videos, but couldn’t finish it all due to my impatience. I love the way he explains about the makeup in depth, the basics & the core elements of different products.

I also kept watching @hudabeauty 15 Sec Contour videos of herself & other artists, she had featured. It really helped me understand the core of contouring. Her journey has always been inspiring to me.

Gradually, I started practicing makeup, made mistakes & kept pushing myself to learn from them. One of the best ways that helped me learn from my mistakes was, taking pictures & correcting what went wrong. Very frustrating, but rewarding process.

I’m blessed & forever grateful for where I am today. Still aspiring to grow & will continue sharing my journey.

.

My creepiest/funniest story with Hailey goes like this:

In downtown Portland, there’s this really cool nature park right in between all these fancy condos. The park has plants that are indigenous to the region and even a pond with fish.

I took the kids there one day and they were both leaning out off the walkway looking down at the fish. Never one to miss a photographable moment, I told them to stay still so I could take a picture. Hailey, age 6 at the time, sighed and rolled her eyes.
.
“I don’t want you to take my picture. Take a picture of the fish.”
.
“Hailey, honey, I don’t want to take a picture of the fish. The fish aren’t my daughter.”
.
And she walks over to me, leans in real close and whispers in my ear:
.
“One of the fish is your daughter.”
.

10 days in NICU 💔
.
It’s a daunting task to pump every 3 hours, deliver the pumped milk to the NICU, spend a few hours with Alyssa - feeding her (when she is capable to take the bottle/breast which isn’t every time) and bonding with her anyway I can, return home without her, care for 2 other little ones, and do it all over again each day. Thus, every time we get updates on Alyssa from the NICU nurses & doctor, we are always inclined to ask, “so how long do you think it will be before she can come home?” And that’s when we are reminded she still has a long way to go before she can. [Check the blog for her week-old updates I just posted]
.
We have to remind ourselves even though she’s 10 days old today, she’s technically only 35 weeks and 6 days (gestation - born at 34 weeks and 3 days). There’s a lot of growth that’s suppose to happen during pregnancy around this time until a baby is full term. Alyssa is doing it all on her own. Our sweet pea little fighter is showing so much strength that I am drawing strength from HER to get by each day myself. ❤️
.

When I was pregnant with Leo, there were times when I felt so overwhelmed with the social and physical burden of pregnancy. My body was splitting apart and I was worried I’d done more harm than good by telling my story. In those darker times, I tried to find a quiet, dark place and just breathe and think about this new life being formed. I imagined he could hear humming, because of its resonance in my chest, and maybe singing. So I would hum and sing softly to him, hoping to somehow connect us so I could keep going.
.
I sing the same songs to him now when he’s sick or wakes up in the middle of the night and can’t get back to sleep. I hold him and sing softly to him and remember when I willed him into being— when I forced myself to keep breathing, keep being, keep sharing... and we both lived to tell the tale.
.
There was a time when you let me know
What’s really going on below
But now you never show it to me, do you?
Well, remember when you moved in me
And the holy dove, that makes three
And every breath we drew was hallelujah
.
Hallelujah,
Hallelujah.
Hallelujah,
Hallelujah.

Жизнь – игра. 
Как часто мы боимся  начинать новое, потому что думаем, что все пойдет не так, как планируем? Перед тем, как взять дело в руки, размышляем, о том, стоит ли оно усилий, ведь «а вдруг не получится?». А представьте, что все это – игра. Вся наша жизнь – игра. На каком-то этапе своего жизненного пути мы сохранились и следуем  дальше. Мы выбираем стратегию, ищем выходы из ситуаций, взвешиваем все «за» и «против». Правда, интересно? 
Мы же помним как в детстве мы легко подходили к понравившемуся человеку и знакомились? Дети не задумываются о результате - дети играют. Они получают удовольствие от жизни и познают ее. 
В любом случае помним о том, что, взявшись за дело, мы набираемся опыта. Если все пойдет не так, мы можем начать заново, уже зная ступени к цели. Нет ничего страшного в ошибках и промахах, потому что всё это так или иначе приведет к какому-то результату. 
Поэтому играйте!

J'ai du partir de mon appart 😭
Tout cest enchaîné très vite
Pour ceux qui ont pas suivi jai des pigeons qui fait leur nid juste derrière la porte de ma chambre qui est condamnée et qui donne sur un couloir extérieur. 
Je trouvais ça mignon au début car voilà ils font des bébés cest chou!
Mais voilà, arrivé à la 2eme ponte (oui ils ont enchaîné, pas le Time) le nid s'est infecté de poux de pigeons. 
Pour ceux qui connaissaient pas comme moi avant que je découvre l'entourloupe en gros cest des insectes qui te bouffent et les piqûres grattent énormément. 
La 1ère nuit j'ai cru que moshie avait des puces
La 2eme nuit j'avais commencer à en voir mais je me suis dis que c'était des petites bêtes inoffensives bah jai pas dormi de la nuit 
Le matin j'étais couverte de piqûres. 
L'après midi elles avaient disparue. Grosse erreur de ma part d'avoir cru que jen étais débarrassée sans lever le petit doigt. 
La 3eme nuit fut la plus horrible mentalement. Je les sentais se balader partout sur moi meme quand cetait pas le cas. 
Après une nuit casi blanche je suis partie acheter des nouveaux draps et une bombe. Bombe avec laquelle je me suis asphyxiée car je n'avais pas compris que c'était un spray qui s'activait et qu'on devait laisser agir dans la pièce. 
Bref je me suis dis que c'était bon. 
Erreur encore une fois car certaines ont apparemment muté et ont continué à me manger la nuit qui suivit. 
Craquage mental total le lendemain après très peu de sommeil cumulé. 
Jai pas eu le choix que d'appeler un spécialiste pour désinfecter mon appart. 
Pas d'autres choix que de se débarrasser du nid et des bébés. 
Du coup on les a fait bouillir tranquille. Nan jdeconne. 
Pour ceux qui savent pas, déplacer le nid reviendrait à la même chose que de les tuer. Une fois l'odeur humaine imprégnée sur le nid la mere abandonne ses petits. 
Il était hors de question que je laisse les bébés à l'abandon ou d'accepter que la personne venu désinfecter mon appart s'en "occupe". Le nid étant le foyer des poux de merde la je n'avais pas le choix... A suivre (y'a plus de place)

•🇪🇸 Hoy hemos descubierto este precioso pedacito de Rumanía, el lago Santa Ana. Es uno de los pocos lagos de Europa formado en el fondo del cráter de un volcán ya apagado. ¡Maravilloso! *Fuente: Google + carteles de los alrededores.
Aparte, en este sitio peculiar ¡¡¡hay osos (y no solo osos...)!!! ¿Y a que no sabéis quién se llevó un susto de muerte mientras iba a repetir esta foto😣? Estaba enfocando y de repente Octa: “¡el, oso, el oso!” Obvio, pensaba que me estaba tomando el pelo, pero cuando me di la vuelta...🤭 una mamá osa con sus dos bebés a menos de 20m. Lo peor de todo es que no debes correr (que es lo primero que se te pasa por la cabeza), sino irte despacito intentando pasar desapercibido. ¡Menuda aventura! Y esta fue la primera del día, igual os cuento más adelante el resto.🤗
•🇷🇴 Astazi am descoperit acest coltisor din Romania numit Lacul Sfanta Ana. Este unul dintre putinele lacuri din Europa format pe fundul craterului unui vulcan stins. Minunat! *Sursa: Google + panourile din jurul locatiei.
Pe langa asta, sunt ursi (si nu numai...)!!! Ghici cine s-a speriat de moarte cand incerca sa repete aceasta poza?😣 In timp ce focusam incepe Octa: “ursu’, ursu’”! Evident, am crezut ca vrea sa ma sperie, insa cand m-am intors...🤭 o ursoaica cu doi puisori la mai putin de 20m. Lucrul cel mai prost este ca nu ar trebui sa o iei la fuga (chiar daca doar asta iti trece prin cap), ci sa te retragi incetisor. Pentru mine a fost o super aventura! Si asta a fost doar prima, poate o sa va mai povestesc si restul zilei cu alta ocazie.🤗 .

앰비언트 스트롭 블러쉬는 약간 오렌지 빛이 나는 컬러인데 되게 예쁘더라고요. 저는 그 핑크색 파우더랑 같이 쓰고 있는데 색감이 둥 뜨지 않아서 완벽쓰..ㅠㅠㅠ국내외 뷰티유튜버와 블로거들이 추천한 이유가 요기잉네.. 저 저번에 신세계 강남점 갔다가 구매해온 거 아시죠? 매장은 신세계백화점 강남점, 신세계면세점 명동점, 신세계면세점 강남점 이렇게 세 군데에서 만나보실 수 있어요.(그나저나 하이라이터 셀카에서도 핑크빔 쏘는 거 실화...?)

Since I haven’t done one of these post in forever I thought why not ? Here is a picture of my hair while transitioning. People are like you wore it like that ? Yes, I wore it just like that. I was in the middle of transitioning and I was definitely very new to natural hair so I just wore it out looking all crazy! At one point I cared about what people thought about my hair because even I thought I looked crazy but then I just got to the point where I didn’t care . If I could go back with the knowledge I know now I would definitely probably do more styles while transitioning but my hair is amazing so I also wouldn’t change a thing. While transitioning I used minimum heat , yes I still used but I definitely shouldn’t have because it wasn’t doing anything but damaging my hair. I stopped getting relaxers all together and I started cutting off 2 inches every 3 months until one day I did a bigger chop to finish off the rest of my damage hair which was back in November 2016! After cutting that damage I straightened my hair a couple more times until May of 2017 when I completely stopped using heat all together. Another thing you want to keep up with is Trims ! I usually get trims every 3-5 months and that’s what helps with hair growth and getting rid of your dead ends even after being fully natural! My journey was long , hard and took a lot of patience but I did it and so can you! Anyone who needs any tips let me know down below ! The first picture was taken March 2016 and my hair now !! My hair is healthy , defined and growing more and more each day. Going natural was definitely the best thing I’ve ever done. Not only does my hair look better but I feel more confident! I want to know about y’alls hair journey down below 🌀💙

Propomel é uma pomada de Própolis e Mel e tem a função de hidratar e suavizar áreas ressecadas da pele. Eu já aplico nos meus lábios todos os dias a noite antes de dormir e meus lábios acordam suaves e brilhantes, já usei nas cutículas quando estão secas. Porém, para minha surpresa, usei um dia quando o Léo estava com uma grande assadura ( Bumbum e Virilha), o alívio e recuperação da pele foi mais rápida do que qualquer outra  pomada com indicação para assadura que eu já havia usado. Então, se você tem um bebê que está com assadura te recomendo demais usar PROPOMEL. O resultado vai te surpreender. Heute möchte ich euch zwei Produkte auch der @pixibeauty Rose Reihe vorstellen. Ich hatte jetzt einige Zeit um die Produkte durch zu testen und konnte mir ein gutes Bild von den Produkten machen. Die Pixi Rose Ceramide Cream ist eine intensiv feuchtigkeitsspendende Creme, die die Elastizität der Haut verbessern soll und Feuchtigkeit spenden soll. Man kann sie täglich oder wie ich nach Bedarf verwenden. Meine Haut braucht nämlich nur manchmal so eine intensive Creme, wie zum Beispiel an manchen Tagen im Winter. Dann aber pflegt sie meine Haut richtig gut und meine Haut kann sich schnell erholen. Die Creme ist für alle Hauttypen geeignet. Die Creme soll man nach der Reinigung und dem Toner anwenden. Sie hat eine pasten ähnlich Texture, die sich leicht auftragen lässt, aber etwas länger braucht bis sie vollständig eingezogen ist, weshalb ich sie lieber abends verwende. Da sie so reichhaltig ist, reicht mir eine kleine Menge, so hält die Creme auch lange. 
Beim Pixi Rose Oil Blend handelt es sich um ein Gesichtsöl, was gut nach Rose riecht. Man kann es sowohl abends als auch morgens verwenden. Am Anfang konnte ich die Pipette nicht verwenden, da die Flasche so voll mit Produkte war, dass die Pipette nicht mehr rein gepasst hat. 🙈 Die Konsistenz ist ölig, trotzdem zieht das Produkt schnell ein und hinterlässt keinen Fettfilm auf der Haut. Das Produkte ist für normale Haut und ist nicht so reichhaltig wie die Rose Ceramide Cream. Das Öl soll Feuchtigkeit spenden, die Haut schützen und sie geschmeidiger machen. 
Das Gesichtsöl habe ich regelmäßig verwendet, da es mir sehr gut gefällt. Ich habe aber keinen großen Unterschied an meiner Haut entdeckt.

Die drei neuen Produkte enthalten alle Gänseblümchen-Extrakt, dadurch wirken die Produkte entzündungshemmend, zusätzlich werden Poren verkleinert und das Hautbild verfeinert.
Das Set besteht aus einem Reinigungsschaum, welcher die Haut von Schmutz, Make-up, Talg und Schweiß befreit. Der Schaum ist etwas fester und lässt sich schön auf der Haut verteilen. Wie alle Produkte, riecht er sehr leicht und angenehm. Der Reinigungsschaum kann man morgens und abends verwenden.
Das zweite Produkte ist ein Gesichtswasser, welches man nach der Hautreinigung verwendet. Damit entfernt man letzte Rückstände und die Haut wird für die nachfolgende Pflege vorbereitet. 
Ganz interessant finde ich hier den Pumpspender. Das Watte-pad braucht man nur draufzulegen und zu pumpen. Sehr einfach und eine praktisch Idee.

CAN YOU REALLY SEE THE DIFFERENCE IF YOU DIDN’T READ THE ANSWERS ON THE PHOTO? .. So many people are obsessed with Balayage. Believe me, I am too! But it’s definitely not for everyone. You can get the look of Balayage with more control over unwanted brassy tones by using Foiling Techniques with a Root Shadow to erase Foil lines. 
Who is a great candidate for balayage? 
Someone who doesn’t mind warm tones left behind and a warm (not brassy) transition area. Balayage shifts hair slowly and will give the least amount of color change in one session. As sessions continue, you will build “NATURAL” brightness creating a multi-level, multi-tonal dimensional look leaving both warm and icier tones. 
Who isn’t 🚫❌a good candidate for Balayage? 
The Client who is extremely dark and wants a very bright icy or ashy end result. ..
Foiling involves small weaves or slices utilizing full saturation of each section giving maximum brightness for 1 session. This is the biggest bang for your buck 🙌🏻🙌🏻. For those of you that say I want it as light as we can get it and I hate gold, yellow or warmth then Foiling is actually the better option 💯✅
Before reading the technique on the pictures would you be able to to tell the difference? 
Trust your stylist to get you the look you want using the right technique. 
Both guests are a level 5 with multiple sessions in these pictures. Ana (left pic) has previously had balayage and opted for the foil for this session to get as light as we could make her and bring her blonde up higher. Both happen to lift very easily using balayage as my technique but took several sessions in these pictures 🙏🏼🙌🏻🥰 Both toned with @schwarzkopfusa Igora Vibrance 9,5-21 and the root shadow in the pic on the left is 8-11 and 7-4 with 6 volume Gel Developer.

Por primera vez en mucho tiempo nos quedaremos en casa para las fiestas de año nuevo. Tenemos mucho trabajo pendiente, viene familia de fuera, y queremos usar estos días para tocar piso nuevamente después de un año de muchos cambios: primer año después de haber vendido nuestra empresa, un embarazo, nacimiento de bebé, colegio nuevo de hijo grande, dejar el pañal, mucho trabajo en general para ambos etc.
Desde que nació Bruno hace casi 4 años hemos tenido muchos cambios en nuestra vida. Hoy, nuestro primo de Alemania al despedirse nos dijo algo muy cierto: "ahora ya tendremos un poco más de estabilidad y podemos planear otras cosas ". Siento que es verdad. Desde hace 4 años, siempre que estabamos a punto de empezar algo nuevo, esto se mezclaba con el nacimiento de un hijo y todo lo que conlleva. Como buena sagitario, me emocionan y me encantan los cambios...pero siento que estoy lista para un poco más de estabilidad para este 2019. Creo😅. #hello2019

.

I often think about Alyssa’s #NICU stay. It was the longest and hardest 34 days of all of our lives. But what if it could have been shorter? Maybe if I’d heard about @prolacta_bioscience while Alyssa was still in the NICU, it could have made a difference. Check the blog for more information, as I’ve partnered with #Prolacta on this #sponsoredpost to raise awareness about the use of 100% human milk fortifier in the NICU. Fortifier is something that’s added to breast milk to provide preemies with the extra protein, calories, and nutrients they need (breast milk alone is not enough).
.
The name “human milk fortifier” can be confusing because most are made with cow milk. But Prolacta’s #humanmilkfortifier is formulated from 100% human milk donated by mamas who have excess breast milk so #preemies get the extra boost they need to thrive.
.
If you’re a #preemie parent like me, or you have family or friends who are, be sure to share this or tag them in the comments below so they can learn more about the benefits of fortifier made with 100% human milk for their baby. And follow my link in bio to head to the blog to learn more.

Considerada uma das instituições de ensino mais modernas na Região Tocantina, a Faculdade Vale do Aço (FAVALE), tem apresentado um projeto inovador na área de educação, desde que foi implantada no município de Açailândia, há três anos.

Com cinco cursos em andamento, e mais cinco previstos para entrarem na grade em 2018, a instituição enumera a lista de compromissos que abarca de 2017 a 2020, no que tange a educação de qualidade. 
Os compromissos traçados pela FALAVE vão desde acessibilidade completa aos seus alunos e colaboradores, passando pela ampliação das instalações físicas, em atendimentos aos novos cursos que entram na grande no ano que vem, já protocolados pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC). A FAVALE, fiel ao seu compromisso, aumentou a qualificação e titulação do seu corpo docente (mestres e doutores). Outro ponto que cabe destacar, é que em apenas três anos de funcionamento, a instituição de ensino, já oferece cinco cursos de graduação e tem aprovação nota 4/5 pelo MEC. É por esses motivos, que a faculdade é referência em educação na Região Tocantina. 
A FAVALE fica localizada na Rod. BR-222, km 02, Jardim de Alah, em Açailândia.  Telefones: (99) 3538-2162 / 99141-4544.

When I'm a home, I'm a mom, farmer's wife & blogger. My girls watch my take pictures & videos to share with my audience. My oldest asked me this morning what her sister's curl type was and what kinds of products work for it. We've had casual conversations about it in passing, do it was funny to me the interest she took in it. Not only did she want to know what works for her sister's 2C hair, but she wanted to know specific product brands 🙌🏾
But then the conversation ended with..my hair is longer because I'm older right 😂

.

Story time:
Being a model since a young age I was constantly fighting for a spot with several girls eventually women and if I didn’t have the support system I did (thanks mom) I can see how thing could have taken a turn for me.
Even with that, it seems like it’s implanted on our brains to constantly judge ourselves.
How many times haven’t we all flipped through a magazine and said “ugh, I wish I had her body - skin - height”
How many time of us haven’t looked at another woman and said “I wish I was as pretty as her”
This year I vowed to love myself again.
Once you realize that other people’s perception of you literally doesn’t change who you are, the doors to self love start to open.
If you are not happy with your body, looking at other women and wishing you look like them will absolutely do nothing for you.
Think about what your body has endured.
My body has made through tremendous losses
My body gave birth to two beautiful children
My body has helped me run after my dreams
My body is my home
Look at YOURSELF in the mirror and say:
I’m abundant
I’m beautiful
I’m strong
I’m the one who designs my own happiness
I can
I will
I am not what have happened to me
I will never let another woman talk herself down, not in my presence! We have enough people out there doing that for us already.
I vow to uplift myself and anyone around me.
Be kind to yourself

This pain has done nothing but prison me from experiencing the joy in my life now. The little girl I speak of is the past version of myself. By revealing this to you all, I hope to find the strength and support I will need.For the last few years I’ve made it a priority to tell the truth about my feelings to others. I was all about holding everyone accountable for what they did not protect me from as a child, what they subjected me to as a teen, and how they made me feel in my present state as a woman. Now, while all this is happening, I realized I was not holding myself accountable for dwelling in this state. I wept and sobbed in my BF’s arms two nights ago because the pain of letting go is too hard. How can I let me go? Everything that was done to me created the person that I am. I was let down so much - I can’t let myself down. I made it my mission to protect and work so hard for the little girl that was stolen from me. This is when I realized, I never really grew up. My whole over-18-years-old adult life has been to make up to the “Brittanie” that didn’t have love. The little girl who was raped by someone who was supposed to be her family. The girl who was neglected and abused by parents and made to feel guilty for her own existence. The teenager, who at 15, almost failed school because she was sleeping in class; tired from working to pay bills. — I wanted to give her everything. — BUT, I realized by doing this, I was the one now stealing from myself. This time, it is the grown woman I am now. I’ve devoted so much of my life trying to make right, trying to nurture, trying to care for the girl that was neglected, that I forgot about me. The Me, I am now. I spent all my adult life trying to make the little girl that I was so proud ...I forgot to be happy. I hate that I felt uneasy about posting this. I hate that the women at the play place yesterday stared at me in judgement as I breastfed my baby while my toddler played. I hate that I have to breastfeed my baby in the car most days we are out. I hate that I have to cover my baby with a wrap at a restaurant when he wants to eat making him feel so uncomfortable, pulling away at the fabric because he can’t breathe. Today, a light ignited inside me. We need to advocate more for breastfeeding in public. Feeding a baby with your own body is beautiful. It’s natural. It’s the way God intended babies to be fed. There was no formula a million years ago. I’m not hiding to feed my baby anymore. I’m not letting those staring eyes bother me. I’m doing the absolute best for my baby and anyone who wants to judge when I do so in public can go right ahead. #normalizebreastfeeding

Today, I felt pretty bad a$$. I have a terrible cold, I’m almost half way through my pregnancy and I have a very active toddler to take care of but there was no “calling in sick” for me (or any full time mothers). We just have to just push through. From the moment we open our eyes to the moment we put our heads on the pillow, we are mothering, wifing, and running the machinery of the home. I’m constantly impressed by how much we can take on. I felt awful but got some fresh air anyway because it’s almost 60 degrees (finally) and well, I relish in watching my boy do what makes him happy.

Mornings with my boys. You guys, poor Richie is so sick and all Ryder wants is his attention. He hasn’t left his bed all morning/afternoon. It’s the first time Richie’s been sick since having Ryder and OMG, dividing my attention between the two has been so hard. This is when I wish I had another set of hands. Hoping my sweet babe feels better soon.

My husband went to work today for the first time since the baby was born. I was a wreck this morning. Petrified to have two kids alone and sad our time together has come to an end. I was so high on the “we just had a baby” paternity leave but the moment Richie kissed his baby brother, danced for him and covered him up in this morning, I knew it would be ok. Even for a few moments at a time. I’m sharing a photo and video (swipe right) that a friend took of my husband and Richie last week. He was seriously super Dad, taking him out every single day so I could care for the baby and just helping out so much. I’m so grateful to have such an amazing man in my life. A huge enormous  shoutout to single moms and those that do it all alone, you are the real heroes in this world.

There are no words to describe the level of guilty of feel. This pregnancy hasn’t been easy but I was still able to push myself to get out for Richie so he can enjoy fresh air, play dates and the beach. Two weeks ago, I was hospitalized because I thought I was in labor. I had to drive myself to the hospital with Richie in the car because my husband works in the city and commutes on the train. It was so scary, you guys. Turns out I was having contractions every two minutes because I was super dehydrated and needed three bags of fluids. I have not felt right since then. My body aches, Braxton-Hicks have been out of control and oh, the headaches. I want so badly to do things with my sweet boy before the baby gets here but I feel terrible. I’m also petrified to leave the house and get dehydrated again or that something else will happen. I’m sharing my story so that any other mamas pregnant in this heat will remember to take care of themselves just as much as they do their little ones. I thought I was drinking enough but clearly wasn’t and like most mamas, my son was my priority. I’m also sharing because I don’t know how to deal with the guilt. I cry thinking about my boy. This is the last month we’ll have together - just us. I miss this time we have already. My heart just aches.

This has got to be the most #raw and hardest post to upload...
But let me be the first to tell you gals that #weightloss isn’t everything.
Sometimes taking life in your hands throwing what you have of it and opening a new chapter to #health #wellbeing #selflove and #selfappreciation is the key to literally all things clarity and happiness.
Why am I so passionate about food?
Because I was actually on my death bed with my legs not being able to move, my lungs almost collapsing and kissing my eyesight goodbye once upon a time, a time where I thought food was the enemy.
I feel absolutely stupid for this post.
But it’s something I’ll take on board to let my #sistas know that fad unhealthy unrealistic diets almost cost me my life and my future.
I was being selfish.
To me.
To my future kids.
To my parents and my sister.
To the ones who loved and cared for me but most importantly I was being a horrible person to my body.
During this - I’ve lost my period. My mental clarity. I’ve almost lost the chance to have kids! I’ve lost many job opportunities (I’m happy with my job now though 🙌🏼👩🏻‍💻) ive lost friends and lost the trust of one too many family members.
Most importantly I’ve lost myself within it.
#annorexianervosa almost cost me my life.
A battle that was 8-9 years long 😔
These two photos is literally a year and a half apart, with a 15kg difference 
It took a lot of #mentalhealth and a lot of courage to bring on overcoming this.
And packing on the weight.
All in all, I did it for my family, friends, my job, my partner, my future kids, and me.
If you really want me to get in depth let me know in a dm or comment below for a video explaining my battles. Damn man. Not my typical post but I wanna share this... Two years ago I was this skinny little thing at 6 months postpartum. I was working full time, breastfeeding, and barely eating, ONLY doing cardio, and I was in a really unhappy headspace. And I was obsessed with being as skinny as possible.
.
.
The pictures on the right I took last week. My body may not be your “ideal body” but it’s my fcking body. And the main thing I had to let go of to get here was THE IDEA OF EVERYONE ELSE’S IDEAL BODY. You can keep that shit. Do I weigh the most I have ever weighed? Yes. Do I give a shit about that number? No. Am I the strongest I have ever been? Yes. I rarely do cardio. I’m lifting weights 6-7 days a week. It’s my favorite form of therapy. Don’t get it twisted, I’m not done here and I’m not trying to seek validation. This is less than a year of lifting. What I’m trying to do is share a simple message to all the skinny-obsessed people - I was there and I STILL thought I was fat. Two years ago I was so low that my best never would’ve been good enough for me anyways. And I do still deal with body dysmorphia, but the stronger I grow physically, the stronger I grow mentally. If we are too hard on ourselves every day and talk about our bodies poorly and talk about ourselves poorly we will never, ever grow in any way, shape or form. Idk I guess what I’m trying to say, in some roundabout way and as corny as it is; don’t give up on yourself, believe in yourself and stop giving a shit about what society tells you you need to look like or be like. And mental growth and strength is as powerful as physical and can catapult you towards greater success. See my instastories to see why my blood is boiling. 
Every child needs a safe place to rest. A place they can let down their guard and process their thoughts and desires. A place to dream and just be a child. Schools are not intended, nor fully equipped, to provide this safe haven. Family life is facing new challenges previous generations never dealt with. The need for parents to step up their game has never been at a higher premium. The stakes are high. Mothers today, more than ever, need to be fierce, strong willed and deliberate. I think women today are stronger and smarter than ever. I really think we have the muscles for this job! Mothers are necessary for our future health. Isn’t it ironic that more now than ever, mothers are questioning their validity and ability? I want to scream “rally!” I want to shout to my fellow troops, “You’ve got this!” It isn’t about fulfilling our needs. Our needs for fulfillment and satisfaction and recognition will be filled as we come to better understand what we are REALLY doing. We are not wiping noses. We are teaching confidence. We are not folding piles of laundry. We are clothing the next generation. We are not cleaning house. We are providing sanctuary. We are not making dinner. We are nurturing souls. 
Strong women wanted. The weak need not apply. 
Rant over.

Too often groups in society who are oppressed get silenced. So in honor of Martin Luther King Jr., here are some social justice issues that matter to me that I feel like sharing.
1. Mental health. 1 in 4 people suffer from a mental illness, but only 1 in 5 of those suffering get help. And access to mental health care providers is disproportionate to income, and poverty is where the highest rate of mental health issues occur. What can you do to help? Be supportive. Stop the stigma. Share any place where others can access help, because there are so many people not getting help they need. 🧠💜
2. The wage gap is still real, ladies. Women make 80 cents for every dollar a man makes, and for women of color, the wage gap is even worse. Mothers make 70 cents to the dollar of fathers. And that just is not fair. What can you do to help? Support legislators in support of the paycheck fairness act. Support family leave (fathers and mothers) and paid sick leave policies so everyone is encouraged to take care of themselves and families, and mothers aren’t punished. Punish sexual harassment and gender discrimination in the workplace (that push women out and stop protecting offenders). Ask for help to negotiate. And don’t ever settle for less than you’re worth!!! ✨💪🏼
3. Education. I will always fight for low income kids to have equal access to a quality education. 14% of kids growing up in poverty graduate college vs 60% of affluent peers. How can you help? Tutor. Volunteer. Donate supplies or books to low income schools. Fund field trips. All kids deserve a chance to pursue their dreams! 🍎

#sponsored I’ve partnered with @COUNTRYFinancial to share my top 5 ways to stay on budget during the holiday season:
⭐️Plan ahead. Make your gift lists and holiday expenses in advance so you can start to set money aside specifically for the holidays. This way, the extra money doesn’t sneak up on you!
⭐️Stop using credit cards and use cash! They’re dangerous! I’ve learned this the hard way, and with the tips from COUNTRY Financial, I’m getting back on track. 🤞🏻💳
⭐️Shop around for the best sales or similar off-brand items. There are TONS of sales, and I rarely buy anything full price.
⭐️Think about purchasing gifts for the holidays all year round and saving them. I shop the summer and post-holiday sales and save items for Hanukkah. Then I’m not spending hundreds of dollars all at once, and I can get the best deal.
⭐️Gift your kids experiences where you can get the most out of your money all year long. Memberships to museums or magazines are favorite gifts of mine. Our whole family loves the outings, and the gift is used for the entire year🙌🏻.

Today was a long one 😅
Up before 7, lots and lots of tears, very little sleep... It was one of those days 😭
It's in these moments where my patience is tested and my capacity is stretched. I failed several of the patience tests today and my capacity felt like it was worn thin. And then when he finally fell fast asleep in my arms after soooo many failed sleep attempts, the mom shame started to creep in:
"You're such an impatient mother."
"He's just a baby. Why are you losing your patience?"
"You wasted your whole day with your son by being frustrated."
"You're not very good at this."
Lies. Lies. Lies. 
And yet, the voices were loud and for a moment (a long one), I let the shame sit there and dictate my belief about who I was as a mom today - an impatient, frustrated, anxious, and overwhelmed mom. 
It took me a hot minute to finally flush the lies and simply just call today what it was - a rough day. It wasn't a day that defines me as a mother nor was it a picture of what every day is like, or will be like. It was just a rough day. 
Then I let grace rush in like a flood and gave myself permission to feel all that I felt today and allowed myself to be loved in all of it. 
Motherhood can be tough but so often we make it even more difficult by being so hard on ourselves. There will be good days and there will be hard days. Neither of them define who I am as a mother. 
Yesterday the Lord told me, "Why do you think you can screw this up so easily when I've given you everything you need to do this well?"
So I'm just gonna let that sink in tonight and be the best mom that I can be again tomorrow.

Y’all😭 This sweet little smile has been in short supply the last couple of weeks. For those of you who haven’t read my post from last week, Zion has been going through a really tough developmental growth spurt and it’s been hard on everyone😬😭 I was finding myself feeling frustrated, overwhelmed, emotional, and powerless before 10am on a daily basis. I would soak up the encouragement of my fellow mom friends and remind myself that this little phase wasn’t going to last forever. But I just felt like I was in it and completely drowning. Before I went into his room to get him every morning, I was already feeling in over my head. Survival was the name of the game and I felt like I was losing. 
I decided that I needed to start my days differently. Normally, my wake up call is Zion squawking at me to come get him out of his crib, but for the last couple of days, I’ve set my alarm for 6:30am (30-40 minutes before Zion wakes up for the day). I turn on the lamp in the living room, light a candle, make a HOT cup of coffee (or two☕️) and do a bit of mindfulness meditation/devotional reading/talking to the lord/breathing deeply (definitely don’t do much of that throughout the day lately😅). I realized that right now, I need to start my day before his in order to keep my sanity. Rather than allowing the day to control me, I need to take ownership of it myself. 
I asked the Lord what he’s teaching me with this tough little toddler phase. He said, “STRENGTH - inner strength. That chaos could be happening all around you and you would remain strong on the inside.”😭
*sigh* Building strength is painful. It’s stretching and exhausting but the strength that is built will actually be sustainable. I’ve come to realize that I make it about me too much - I’m tired. I’m worn out. I’m overwhelmed. I’m going through this. I’m having a rough day. When I make it all about me, it really is exhausting. Can I have a day/moment where I am just DONE? Yes, absolutely. But when I think on things that are pure, lovely, true, right, and excellent; when I wrap myself in gratitude and thankfulness for what is right in front of me, my perspective shifts and the moments are easier and far more sweet❤

I clean when I’m anxious. I purge my closets when I’m mad. I do laundry when I’m overwhelmed. I organize cupboards when I’m frustrated. 
Some people eat their feelings; other people sleep on them. Some will drink or do drugs to numb their feelings. I, however, scrub, wash, wipe, organize, and launder my feelings aside. I am, what you would call, your classic over-functioner. The more stressed and overwhelmed I feel, the more I do. If one area of my life feels out of control, I’ll do my best to keep every other area of my life in tip top shape. “Wow! What a productive coping mechanism!” you might say. Sure, my house is - 9 times out of 10 - relatively clean and organized. However, when I’m stressed, while I’m scrubbing and folding, my insides are likely dying and because everything looks pretty good on the outside, no one ever usually suspects what’s actually going on on the inside. So while that one girl who constantly shows up late for work when she’s stressed out is checked up on because she’s acting out of character, everyone typically assumes I’m doing pretty great from the outside looking in. 
I’ve had people say they WISH their stress response was like mine. I’ll admit, I truly appreciate and love the part of me that can get stuff done no.matter.what. But, being fully honest, it’s exhausting. And the harder I try and “keep it together,” the more exhausted and overwhelmed I feel. 
My number one strength is “achieving.” Every day starts at zero and “success” looks like, every day, getting as far away from zero as humanly possible. Therefore, I find myself feeling guilty when I put my feet up or take a moment to rest because there’s always more to be done. 
My intention these days is more self-compassion, which is a struggle for me because I set the bar so high at all times. But I’d never expect from other people what I expect from myself (except for my husband sometimes #guilty). Nor would I ever punish them by making them work harder like I often do to myself. 
Anyways, all this to say is that today, after scrubbing the floor on my hands and knees like a crazy person, I’m MAKING myself rest. And enjoy it. And not feel guilty about it. Cause I’m human.

Motherhood has been, by far, the hardest thing I've ever done. It's been a dying and a rebirth of sorts. Surrender has been a daily (sometimes hourly) process - a surrender of my right to have it all figured out and be ten steps ahead of the game like I've always been used to. 
Mom: It's such an overwhelming role and there is so much demand on every part of you - physically, emotionally, spiritually, emotionally. So much required. So much expected. So much needed. You give all of yourself - everything you have and then some. And you're met with sleepless nights, countless moments of tearful frustration, a cold and an unexplained body rash, those extra pounds and that squishy tummy, and the loss of your peaceful evenings with your husband. 
I remember a moment when Zion was a couple days old when I realized I could do it - that I actually had what it took to be his mom and to do it well. But it's been a process of figuring out what that actually looks like... for me. Regardless of what every other mom out there is doing and what all the books say to do. Motherhood is my own journey and it looks completely different from everyone else's journey. Zion is his own person, regardless of what every other infant out there is doing. 
It's been beautifully intense, but then comes the reward: the precious moment when he looked into my eyes for the first time; his first smile and every single smile afterwards; his early morning, mid-afternoon, late night, and middle of the night cuddles; and the realization that I'm his mom... forever. I'm here to change his diapers today and one day I'll be there on his wedding day.
I've continued to say that motherhood is the best and hardest thing I've ever done. You can't understand the tension until you're in it. But with alllllll of that, I wouldn't change a thing. Motherhood has forced me to slow down, to enjoy the moments, to appreciate what actually matters in life, to reckon with my fears and my insecurities, and to be open and honest with where I'm at on a daily basis. 
Motherhood has changed my life ❤️ #ziondupreenelson

People always used to call me “shy.” The word crippled my untapped personality and reduced the very essence of who I was to timid, reserved, small, and hidden. In college, I discovered I was an introvert and hid behind my quietness for years. I soon discovered that the world highlights extroverts and incorrectly assumes their outgoing and dominant nature is what makes them great leaders. Therefore, I spent the next several years trying to be an extrovert. I forced myself to be big, loud, and sociable, all the while dying inside and feeling as though I was betraying my truest self. I hated that I was an introvert. It felt like I was being labeled as “shy” all over again. 
I’m beginning to realize that some of the worlds greatest leaders are quiet, introverted leaders. Their quietness does not diminish their bravery nor does it decrease their confidence. I have grown so tired of putting on an extroverted facade in order to appear legitimate or to appease the people around me. 
I am an introvert. I love people, but my energy comes from spending time alone. I have been described as poised, still, professional, peaceful, strong, and regal, all of which are qualities I admire in many of the strong, introverted leaders I look up to. 
I say this because I feel like some of you needed to be given the permission to be yourselves. I feel like you needed to be liberated from the beliefs and opinions people have about your quiet strength. You are free to stand in the corner of the party and socialize with just one or two people; to lead alongside those who are loud and outgoing and be okay with not saying much, just because you don’t want to; to be in a group and not feel the pressure to speak up as much as everyone else around you. Don’t let the beliefs and ideals of others dictate how you are expected to be, act, engage, and interact. Be you. That’s all that was ever asked of you. Be you, in all of your quiet and beautiful strength.

This week, I found myself feeling really restless. That kind of anxious restlessness in your soul that keeps you from really enjoying anything that’s going on😬 I took an inventory of my life and came to the conclusion that there had to be something going on on the inside of me. I was mindlessly scrolling through Instagram and stumbled across a post about someone who was talking about being present, but not actually being PRESENT.⁣⁣
• ⁣⁣
As a high-achieving, task oriented, image conscious enneagram 3, I can get pretty wrapped up in whatever it is that I NEED to or SHOULD be doing — “I need to get some work done... I should be doing laundry... I could be getting something else done...”🙄 The narratives in my head are often written around what’s expected of me... from myself. I expect myself to be further along than I am and so I spend my moments trying to figure out how to get there instead of being where I am. ⁣⁣
•⁣⁣
I realized yesterday that because I’m so caught up in what I’m NOT doing, that even though I’m present with what’s in front of me, I’m not actually PRESENT. I’m not actually there at all, which is exactly why I wasn’t enjoying myself. ⁣⁣
•⁣⁣
My word for 2019 is to be PRESENT - but being present isn’t just showing up physically. If I’m there in the flesh, but my mind is trying to get something else done, I’m not actually PRESENT. ⁣⁣
I share this because I felt like some of you are present, but you’re not really showing up. You’re too busy trying to be somewhere else in your mind while the present moment that’s right in front of you is drifting away. ⁣⁣
•⁣⁣
Check your heart. Are you being present with your life? Are you showing up? Are you checking out? Are you escaping? Look down at your life instead of ahead and around. Don’t miss out on the beautiful life that’s right in front of you!⁣❤️

I spent the entirety of my teenage years and a chunk of my young adult years running away from myself and desperately attempting to be someone else. Comparing myself to everyone around me, I sought to be smarter, funnier, extroverted, and more desirable in every sense of the word. I truly believed there was something inherently wrong with the way I was made and so, instead of being myself, I was bits and pieces of everyone else. 
I found myself exhausted and miserable from walking hundreds of miles in everyone else’s shoes over the course of nearly two decades. I had no idea who I was or what I liked. I embodied the preferences, opinions, and qualities of so many different people - friends, boyfriends, parents, celebrities, the media, you name it. 
I have since then been on a journey of unraveling the false persona I had built up over those many years. I am piecing back together the ME I had been ashamed of and embarrassed about for so long. 
It’s been a long, sometimes tiresome, and extremely intentional process but the fruit of being myself is FREEDOM - freedom to discover, know, and be ALL of myself!
Let me just say this, you were created to be YOURSELF. “Just be yourself” is a cliche phrase, but you exist to be just that - your fun, quirky, introverted, loud, crazy, passionate, brilliant, lighthearted, driven, creative self. 
The End.

As an enneagram 3 and a high achiever in every sense of the word, I struggle with disappointment sometimes, particularly disappointment with and in myself. Disappointment for not hitting the mark, not getting enough done, not achieving the way I planned, not meeting my expectations... the list goes on. 
The disappointment feels like anxiousness and restlessness in the pit of my stomach and it makes me want to (1) achieve even more or (2) the complete opposite and shut down, shut out, and self-medicate with TV, chocolate, or organizing something (yeah, I know, it’s weird. Lol). Today, I felt all that in the pit my stomach - that old familiar feeling of disappointment for not achieving what I wanted to. I felt it all day, dictating the posture of my heart and leaving me disassociated rather than present. 
So tonight, I’m throwing a huge blanket of grace over myself and hurling kindness and compassion at my heart like my life depends on it. And honestly, it’s the least I’ve “achieved” all day and it feels pretty good. 
Anyone else need to overdose on some compassion today? ❤️

bath bombs that make your bath water look like mud, smell the best alright 🙃 I haven’t posted any content in a while because I’ve been sick which then triggers all of my MS symptoms which then makes me even more sick ~ a vicious cycle ~ but I’m still here, wurking behind the scenes 💞 chronic illness has no days off & I’m not about to force it/take pictures and pretend like it does 🤷🏽‍♀️.

What you see VS what you don’t 💓 I often get comments both online and in real life saying things like “You don’t look sick” and although I know it’s never meant maliciously, (more like a compliment) I’d like to remind you that not all disabilities are visible and even behind big cheesy smiles like this, sometimes there’s a lot of struggle and pain. 👎🏼 Millions of people worldwide are living with a chronic illness and many of these diseases cannot be seen by the naked eye. The worst thing you could do is make them feel like they have to prove how sick they are. 🤦🏽‍♀️ This is where my big mouth comes into action because I promise you, I will NEVER stop talking about it. 🧡💪🏽 There are good days, bad days, overwhelming days, tired days, I’m fine days and I can’t go on days.. but everyday I make it through. Becoming a mom of two has definitely been a roller coaster of emotions. In the beginning I felt like I was failing and missed that one on one time with my first born. It was a big adjustment for everyone.  Often times I would find myself looking at other mamas of multiples and wondering how the heck did they make it look so easy.. I wish I could clone myself in times like that and send a more put together version to give her the attention she deserves. On those bad days, I felt myself weighed down by that guilt and was scared that my babies would only see me as a mama who lost her freakin' marbles during this transition rather than the mother that takes the time to adore and enjoy them. 
But, as the weeks turn into months, I realize I am starting to win more rounds than I lose. And I know that I am trying, with every beat of my heart, to be someone they can look up to.

So, while there is chaos, a lot of juggling, and some days tears, there is also so much love and so much joy. And the moments when Evie just wants to entertain or love on her baby brother, and I see Forden look at her with so much wonder and adoration, my heart just bursts and I think “This! **Birth Story Part 2 ** I waddled myself to the bathroom and even more water continued to break over the toilet. Having a baby is never glamorous haha. I remember apologizing for my water dripping on the way to the bathroom, and they were like, "honey please.. that's nothing".. and in retrospect they were so right.

Now the contractions definitely were stronger as there was no more liquid 'cushion' anymore.. around 1pm the nurse had asked if I wanted the epidural and though I was really wanting to say yes, I declined at the time because it made me feel like I was actually doing something and feeling like I was dilating faster if that makes any sense. The pain gave me confidence that I was progressing. I was worried that if I couldn't 'feel'  the contractions anymore that I would just stay at 4cm forever and basically just go into the Guinness World Book of Records for 'expecting mama stays at 4cm for 2 more years".. I told you, I was very irrational. From 1-2pm that was definitely the toughest  in breathing through the contractions now that they were coming every 2-3 minutes. Around 2ish I caved & asked for the epidural and thankfully she was up within 10 minutes to administer it. This is where things got a little interesting though. I was nervous from the get go with the epidural just because I remembered last time how it felt going in and needing to stay still and in the 'hug over your bump' position was uncomfortable. So on top of just being anxious for that part I started to cry a little bit and my husband and nurse were so encouraging and said that soon I'd feel better and it would be over in minutes. They were right, the epidural definitely kicked in, but unfortunately not as we all hoped for. My right leg was immediately numb as was my whole right side and I soon realized that something wasn't quite right. (Continued in next post)

** Birth Story Part 3 ** The contractions in my stomach were now just a dull pressure and not painful, but all of a sudden it was like the contractions went from my belly to the left side of my lower back. I was having excruciating back labor now. I told my nurse that it was almost more painful now than before. So she propped pillows up all underneath my right side as we were thinking the epidural was mostly just medicating that side. I could still wriggle my left foot around and pick my left leg up but basically my right leg was literally dead weight and pins and needles and my left back pain was killing me. We waited about an hour to see if all the pillow propping and adjusting would work but finally we agreed that something was wrong and they needed to reinsert the epidural all over again and start over. I wanted to cry hysterically, and I think I did, I tried to block out that part of the experience.. that was probably the worst part of my story.. I tried to relax my body more this time as I really wanted it to work this time and not ever have to go through that again .. the anesthesiologist was so nice and kept talking to me to keep me distracted.. she even announced she was about 12 weeks pregnant and that I was now one of the first people she told it to. She was very sweet. Soon after I finally felt numb on both sides and the contraction pain in my lower back disappeared (hallelujah!).. my body finally relaxed and literally from 3pmish-5pm I went from 4cm to 10cm.. I knew I was ready to start pushing because with both my pregnancies I was nauseous right before I was fully dilated. The nurse had just left the room not even 5 minutes before when I felt like I would be sick so I asked my husband to find me a bucket. He found one in a closet and brought it over, the nurse walked in shortly after and asked if everything was okay and I told her I was going to be sick. She found a bag for me instead and laughed because my husband pulled out the bucket that they use for mothers who wants to take their placenta home haha. Rain rain go away 🌧 
Speaking of rain, January has been a tough month for me. I can’t seem to get my mind in the right place and right when I think I’m almost there, something is raining on my parade. I know it may seem like all bloggers and social influencers are confident and happy and nothing ever goes wrong in their life, but it sure isn’t that way. I like to keep my little space of the internet uplifting, positive, and “joy”ful because my purpose for starting my blog was to create joy in others lives, but I also like to keep it honest. For whatever reason, I’ve felt like giving up on this blog of mine all together recently. I’ve felt like nothing I’m saying or doing is worth it to anyone, the incredibly long nights aren’t paying off, the stress of it all just seemed consuming. I listened to an awesome podcast last night and realized I need to care much less about what others think of me, and just be the me that I like best. The me that wants to help each of you feel less alone and be there to share messages I have on my heart. I had an experience today that solidified to me that if you’re trying to do good, don’t stop. I met a follower’s husband randomly today and was so grateful he stopped me to quickly tell me to keep it up. So now I’m going to tell you guys to keep it up. It may not be a blog, but I guarantee there’s something you’re doing that may be taking up your time and energy, that is absolutely worth it. Maybe it’s raising tiny humans, or big humans. You are literally changing your children’s lives by acting on the impressions you get to teach and inspire them. Maybe it’s a podcast, a job, a friendship, a service project, or supporting those around you. YOU ARE NEEDED! Keep it up, even when you feel like the good you are doing goes unnoticed. If you are trying to do good, it is worth it. So let me pass along a virtual hug to each of you that may have gotten caught in the January blues as well... You are doing a great job, keep on going! 💗

This is how Cam feels about social media currently... but seriously, instagram has been a really toxic place lately and I've just kinda had to take a break. I don't know about the rest of you, but I have a love/hate relationship with this app. It can be such a positive and uplifting place for me to feel inspired and connect with other women. It can also leave me feeling jealous as I compare my life to others. So here's what I have to say about the whole thing to anyone who cares... We're all human, every single one of us, but we also each have strengths in different categories. There is nothing wrong with sharing those strengths and talents here. If you let it be, this app can be used for so much good. It can also become addictive since it plays a huge role in our lives today. Obsessing over social media and making it the sole influence in your life isn't why we have it. Social media is addicting, it consumes our thoughts and actions, and can easily create unreal expectations. And that, is when you need to feel the pull to just put your phone down. I know it's easier said than done, but I promise it'll make a difference. Unfollow people if you wish, but just remember that nobody is required to share every piece of their life to be "real." The fact that people are able to filter out what they do and don't post says a lot about character and boundaries. I have created boundaries for myself on what I post to protect the loved ones in my life. Sure my marriage isn't perfect, sure I struggle with my toddler, yes I have had struggles with friends... but I won't post about those things at the risk of damaging a relationship just to be "real." Everyone's real is different, and that's how it should be. The world would be such a boring place if we all had the same struggles and talents. Just remember, the enemy here is not each other, it is not who you follow or unfollow, it is not the brands for wanting to market their products either! The enemies are the monsters named jealousy and addiction. Shame on anyone who promotes pushing out negative thoughts by putting others down. That will never solve the problem. (More in comments)

She managed to push every one of my buttons today and by the time she got her finger stuck in the Starbucks water cup after I repeatedly told her not to stick her finger in the hole for the straw... I about lost it. I was sitting on the freeway in bumper to bumper traffic and she was screaming at the top of her lungs. Cam then started to scream because hey, why not? Between the screams, my frustration, and Oaklyn’s terrified sobbing... I realized something. As the mom, I have the opportunity to change the mood of a situation. In that situation, I reacted poorly. I was already frustrated because Oaklyn tested me over and over again during our errands. I foresaw what would happen when she first started to stick her finger in the cup. I told her not to, but the kid is three and experimenting/figuring things out for herself are all part of this phase. When she panicked, I chose to react negatively. I took a deep breath and worked really hard to be calm after that. She got her finger out, we talked about the situation, and she apologized for her actions. I couldn’t help but wonder how many other instances could have ended differently if I would have chosen to react differently. Motherhood has taught me a lot in my short 3ish years of doing it, but everyday I learn something new. It’s pretty amazing that these little ones teach us more than we’ll ever teach them. #mamalovesoaks #oaklynjoymoore

Today I realized how tricky it really is to bring two kids to the grocery store when they're little. Cam is too big for my beloved cart hammock now and most carts aren't big enough for two kiddos. (Bless you Costco) I opted for sticking oaks in the basket and cam in the seat. That resulted in a meltdown because "mommy that's my seat not sissy's." Then Oaklyn started making towers with the cans and boxes and burying herself with the produce 🤦‍♀️🤦‍♀️🤦‍♀️ When I got up to the checkout feeling completely crazed, the lady took one look at my girls and went on and on about how adorable they are. Oaklyn was eating it up and cam was giggling away. "You know, you're going to miss this one day. I promise you" she said as I paid for our groceries. I've heard that a zillion times before but today it really hit me. I walked out with Oaklyn searching for the rainbow goldfish in the bag and begging for a lollipop and cam grinning up at me because riding in the cart was basically the time of her life. This time is hard. Oh boy is it hard. The days are really long, and a lot of nights are too. There's a lot of messy diapers, meltdowns (from everyone), snacks in between the seats of the car, Disney movies, potty training accidents, bribes, and second guessing myself... but holy moly I wouldn't change any of it for the world. My two little rascals are my world. Life would be really quite empty without them. Less chaotic for sure, but really empty. So here's to trying not to roll my eyes the next time someone tells me I'm going to miss all this. Because truly, I really think I will. #motherhoodunplugged #motherhoodinspired #motherhoodrising #cambriataylormoore

This girl and I fight all day long. It usually starts with what she’s going to wear for the day and ends with trying to stay up later than I already let her stay up. There’s usually a hundred arguments mixed in throughout the day varying from getting her shoes on to eating her lunch and what song is playing in the car to not getting treats and toys at target. She’s strong willed and sassy and will negotiate as if she’s a lawyer. I know, I know, your toddler is the same way and it’s just a phase... but it’s a really exhausting phase. A mentally exhausting phase. I question myself daily and feel like I’m losing my mind trying to get my point across to a three year old. Some days I go hide in my closet to recollect myself but most days, I just want to throw in the towel. But, I won’t. Because a girl like Oaklyn, with this much drive, passion, and determination to get what she wants is going to make a big difference one day. But, that’s only going to happen if I teach her now how to direct those wonderful qualities she has for good. So to all of you moms out there with your very own “Oaklyn” I’m right there with you about ready to pull my hair out. But in 25 years, I guarantee we’re going to be incredibly proud of who she is becoming, so being that we help them use their strong qualities for good. The world could use a few more strong women ready to make a difference in a gentle way. #oaklynjoymoore #wordsformymoorebabies

This day will always be a day we talk about with our kids. It will also be a day to teach them that our country was able to unite together during such a terrible time. There is power and strength in unity and I hope as we remember that day, we also remember to stand together. 💙❤️ #neverforget #911

Four years ago was my first Mother’s Day with this little lady. I was a brand new 20 year old mother with a baby that screamed most of the day, and suffering from PPD. I remember waking up and feeling like I didn’t deserve to be celebrated. I was having an incredibly difficult transition into motherhood and my mental illness led me to believe I was an inadequate mother. Still, those around me celebrated me, spoke positively of me, and cheered me on. In my mental state, I didn’t believe that it would ever get better. I didn’t believe I would ever feel like “I got this.” Fast forward to now... my 4th Mother’s Day. I so badly wish I could go give 20 year old, brand new mama me a hug and say “just you wait... in a few years that same screaming newborn will be singing songs in her class staring proudly at you the whole time and you’ll have to wipe a  soft tear away as she sits on your lap eating Oreos and apple juice saying you’re the best mom ever.” Motherhood pretty much slapped me in the face and changed me completely 4 years ago. And today, I can easily say it has all been worth it. PPD rocked my world two times over, but I know with every ounce of my being that I’d do it all again for my girls. So if you’re spending your first Mother’s Day having a hard time and wondering if it gets better... I’ll be the first to say it does. The fog will lift, The light at the end of the tunnel will appear, and the tear jerking school performances will come. Oh sweet mama, it will all be worth it. #ppd #ppdsurvivor #happymothersday #postpartumdepression #ppdawareness #postpartumdepressionawareness

Three years ago today I got a phone call that I ignored twice and on the third try I knew in my gut something was wrong. I answered and the voice on the other end said, “Your husband has severely injured his hand cutting a piece of wood with a saw, you need to come down to the hospital immediately.” My heart dropped and I remember feeling like I couldn’t get to him fast enough and when I finally did, he was shaking with pain and shock had finally set in. Looking back, after multiple surgeries and a 4 month long recovery, it was one of the hardest times of our lives but in that same breath one of the most special too. I think back on that time with so much gratitude, I know he was being watched over... later when we saw the glove he was wearing it showed that all of his fingers should have been cut even down into the palm of his hand, it was a miracle he had as little damage as he did. It was so hard seeing him go through not being able to reattach his fingers, getting a bone infection, and a picc line in his arm with a tube going down near his heart for direct antibiotics, but I can honestly say he has never gotten down about it, he’s my hero. We cried and laughed, and talked each other through those months of recovery. We were stretched and grew in ways we didn’t know we could. It truly was such a special time in our lives and is now a part of our family story. 
His left hand tends to be the hand that I hold and is a quick reminder to me how much I love what that trial did for us as individuals, a couple, and as a family. The out reach by others touched our hearts dramatically and I know that God was aware of us and was there through all of it and that He still is now and always will be no matter what. #nogsfingers

Our marriage hasn’t always looked like this. Not many people know this but shortly after the twins were born our marriage was really struggling. To be honest it was kind of hanging on by a thread. During one counseling session in particular, Nog said something that hit me hard and woke me up in a way that I knew I needed to step it up or I’d lose him. I would need to put him above myself and not just for a moment but as a new way of living. I would need to do a complete 180 if I wanted to have the marriage I’d always dreamt of and so I began the process of doing just that. 
I shifted my mindset so that instead of waiting for him to make me happy, I took steps to be in charge of my own happiness because at the end of the day that wasn’t his job, it was mine. 
Taking these steps and shifting my mindset slowly began to change the dynamic of our marriage in ways more incredible than I never could have imagined. 
Fast forward four years later and I can’t believe how far we have come. Every now and then I think about how close we were to losing it all and now here we are with five perfect little children and honestly our marriage has never been happier. Of course we still have our disagreements because we’re human, but I am so incredibly grateful we both had the courage to move forward and not give up on each other when it seemed too hard. Anything worth while isn’t going to be easy, in fact I believe it will be the exact opposite. Be the best you that you can be, have faith, and the rest will follow. You’re the love of my life, Logan. I often get asked “How Much for this picture?” Or “how much for this look?”
I’m here to tell you that Giving you a price based on zero information on your part can’t happen. What’s your starting point? Do you have color in your hair already? What condition is your hair in? Are you on medication? This picture isn’t equivalent to ordering a steak or picking out a new car. 
There are many variables and often previous sessions that go into creating a customized look for each guest. Quoting prices randomly over the internet isn’t my thing. I know a lot of people are curious as to what I charge. I’m high for some and reasonable for others. Telling me I’m too high is the equivalent of me going into your work and telling your boss he pays you too much and you aren’t worth it. It’s insulting. Telling me it’s too much for your budget is completely acceptable and not an insult to me whatsoever. Having your hair done is a luxury service. It’s not a necessity. Please don’t pick out a Maserati if you only have a budget for a Huffy. That doesn’t make me too pricey. Would you walk into a Louis Vuitton and tell them they charge too much for their merchandise? Anyone who finds value in their brand would save their money until they could afford it. “My Hairdresser told me my hair pulls RED 👩🏻‍🦰“ 😬 🤦🏼‍♀️ Here’s why. 
We measure the depth or lightness of hair in LEVELS (10)
Level 1 = BLACK 
Level 5 = Medium Brown 
Level 10 = Palest Blonde 
Each level has underlying pigment. Underlying pigment is exposed when Lightener is introduced. Literally every person on the planet when lightened will show some form of red, red orange, orange or orange yellow unless they are starting at a level 8 or lighter. So let’s break it down. Every level you see on the chart has an underlying pigment located directly opposite. The deeper the shade the more red is present. The lighter the shade more orange to yellow is present. So, IF we are trying to take any of you natural raven haired beauties from a level 2 up to a level 7 we have to lift 5 levels. (Hair color only lifts 4 levels so bleach is needed) Notice that at a level 7 (which is a dark blonde to you) ORANGE/Yellow or better known to you as dreaded GOLD 😱 IS PRESENT. You’ve lifted through 5 full levels of depth to reach this target level. (That’s A LOT)
If you tone at the level 7 achieved, within a few Shampoos the orange remaining pigment will bleed back through & your hair will start showing brassy orange tones. The only way to combat brassy tones in the hair is to EITHER .. 1) Lift past a level 7 to an 8 or 9 and then tone back down to a 7 .. OR 2) sacrifice the brightness from a level 7 and tone down 1 to 2 full levels to control brassiness. Texture and density absolutely make a difference in how easily hair lifts. Coarse thick hair generally lifts very slowly where fine thin hair lifts quite easily. 
Please look at the bottom half of the chart. Do you see the all the orange into red color blocks? In every level but 8 & 9. That’s the underlying pigment at each level that exists naturally. Its present in almost every freakin level!! 🤯🤯 This is why you “pull red”. It’s unavoidable. In most cases clients aren’t light enough & that’s why they’re brassy. Lightening hair takes time and patience & if you’re dark to begin with you will absolutely deal with warm tones while you’re on your blonde journey. I hope this helps explain why you pull ❤️ or 🧡💛

These ingredients are in many many products I used 😫 so I’ve been going through some trial and error these past weeks. I’m here to show you that I’ve triumphed! When Léo was 1,5 years old - me and his father split up for the first time. I was a heartbroken 25 year-old, and in between hours spent looking for a job, preparing for Real Estate exam, being full time mom to Léo, having financial stress and trying to carve a little time for creativity. 
That first year was chaos. It did help that there were single-mom friends in my life - other moms that I knew that were going through “more or less” the same situation. That same year we tried working on our relationship. We both agreed on seeing a couple therapist to help us work on our marital issues. However, even the therapist saw that this marriage wasn’t working. Almost a year passed and I decided that it wasn’t going anywhere and I couldn’t live in misery anymore. The decision was made and I filed for a divorce. Fortunately, I have a fantastic group of friends who helped. Maybe none of them knew exactly what I was going through, but they babysat and showered me with support and respect for being strong, which I appreciate to this day. After a time, I got back on my feet and ventured out. And what did I see? A lot more single moms than I had ever noticed before. Statistics don't tell how many single moms are with a partner (not married), how many live with family (so they can have help), and how many are truly alone. But the point is, there are a lot of single moms out there.

Day-to-day duties for a solo parent are no different than they are for a married one: coping with sleeplessness, child care, paying bills. But... you're on your own. I’m eternally thankful for my parents and I’m thankful for you guys and for all your messages, kind words of encouragement. Another school #shooting just took place few days ago in #Florida. While everyone talks about the #guncontrol (which i agree with), there is also a deeper problem. Guns don’t kill people, people do. These kids are troubled, they must be suffering with severe mental issues. Maybe we need to address that, why does it happen more often? Maybe its the games that we praise and big companies advertise? Maybe its the everyday struggle of working and worrying about paying bills, instead of enjoying family time and paying attention to our children? Imagine sending your kid to school alive and in return you’re receiving a coffin with the corpse. The children are innocent and do not deserve it. In fact no one deserves it. It happened once when i was in school (9th grade). Beslan school hostage started on 1 September 2004, lasted three days, involved the illegal imprisonment of over 1,100 people as hostages (including 777 children), and ended with the deaths of at least 334 people. I remember when the schools were closed and we prayed and hoped they will come to their senses and no one will get hurt. When they let the kids run to their parents they started shooting at their backs. What is wrong with the society? That was a tragedy. We still have to mourn every September 1st to remember what happened then. Now its a “usual thing” it seems. We have to speak with our children, we have to communicate with them, really communicate. To every parent, teacher, and child who is hurting so badly, we are here for you – whatever you need, whatever we can do, to ease your pain. We are all joined together as one American family, and your suffering is our burden also. I really hope a better change for this world is coming, and when its time to send my son to school, there will be no fear in my heart. #presidentsday

BE HUMBLE AF
someone asked me recently if poverty was 'still a thing'. I'm still not sure if she was being facetious or was completely blind to reality. 1 in 4 children in Edinburgh are living in poverty. That's 1 in  4 too many. .
.
We're getting better on the whole at talking about real issues but we've got a long way to go. Money is still a grubby topic for many and this puts pressure on people to keep up a pretence that everything is ok.
.
.
I'm guilty of moaning about being skint when in reality I'm not. I'm not flush but we are fed and clothed with no issues. It doesn't matter how grateful I am though. Do you think someone living under the breadline gives a flying fuck about how grateful I am? I'm guessing not. It's easy to turn a blind eye to poverty, it's tough and it's easier not to see it. Its not pretty.
.
.
Perhaps like me you're financially stable but not enough to donate a great deal to charity. That's ok! Could you donate to a local foodbank? Our school has a uniform swap - could you find out about one or even set one up? I'm a fixer and I believe that everyone deserves the same opportunities. We're a million miles away from that but in order to move forward please look around.
.
.
Be mindful of your situation and that many are in a very different situation. If you're school isn't having a Halloween party with costumes please consider why before you complain. If you think it's awful that all homework isn't emailed please think. We live in a society that takes so much for granted and we all need a reminder just to stop and think sometimes. We don't all have the same resources sadly. .
.
Ask yourself if a friend of yours was really struggling do you create a safe enough place for them to speak about it? So many people aren't aware of support available because they are too proud or ashamed to ask for help. There should be no shame. .
.
Things change so quickly. My past has made me cynical (or a realist depending on how you look at it). Jobs end, relationships break down and health can change quickly. .
.
Be supportive as there might come a time when you need that support. You'll be glad you were humble. ❤
