When I was in my teens, I started suffering from panic attacks. I would simply blackout and wake up in a hospital. My classmates would look at me completely different the next day.
I had no bruises
I had no symptoms
I wasn’t sick, I didn’t sound sick, I didn’t look sick at all
It’s so common, it could be anyone.
The trouble is, nobody wants to talk about it
And that makes everything worse.
It has been many many years since I had a terrible episode like that and I am so thankful for it. I’ve worked hard for it and I still do, everyday. The battles never end.
I used to live my life so afraid, having anxiety about having an anxiety attack while I lived alone or traveled alone or maybe when I would be home alone with my kids.
I still cry, a lot
I get hives all over my body
My heart beats so fast I think I’m going to faint
I have fearful thoughts, everyday.
I have anxiety being in a car
I have anxiety being on a plane
I have anxiety as soon as I drop my son off at school
I have anxiety so I eat, allllllll the things
I have anxiety so I refuse to eat, as if I needed punishment
I’m afraid, everyday
I am triggered by so many things, little things, big things...
Losing family members was a breaking point for me, I thought I was going to literally loose my mind. I still do at times.
I see my oldest son, biting his nails, getting frustrated that things don’t go his way, throwing a fit because his shirt doesn’t match his shoes. And I pray so hard that he will never ever ever grow up to be like me when it comes to that 🙏🏻
I want anyone who’s reading this to know that, anxiety comes in MANY forms and it can also look like absolutely nothing on the outside because it’s something that it’s battled on the inside.
Let’s please help each other and break the stigma that mental illnesses are.
I am stronger because I keep fighting
I am stronger because I am not afraid to talk about my battles, anymore.
Your illness does not define you,
Your strength and courage does ❤️
If you ever need me, I am here.
I mean that.
Wether I know you personally or not,
I am here for you, so you don’t have to be alone
EVER

Can’t let the week get away from me without talking about maternal mental health #mmhweek2019 ! 
I’m a postpartum nurse, I have a ton of family support, I have three healthy babies...and postpartum depression snuck up on me. I have felt lonely, irritable, angry, uncertain, and disconnected from “me”. I have deeply questioned if I made the right decision to become a mom. I have experienced it differently with all three of my children, but I recognize it as only a part of my journey, and not a part of who I am. 
Our minds and bodies are up against so much in the transition to motherhood.  Truly no one can prepare you for what it is like.  It’s okay that motherhood isn’t everything you thought it would be, that sometimes it is so much better but sometimes it is so much harder. It’s okay that you just don’t feel like you anymore. Please don’t hold it in! Your concerns may get brushed off, but keep telling whoever will listen. There is help and you will be well again! Check out postpartum support international and @thebluedotprj for help. 📷 @liaeverettephoto

If I were to write a book about motherhood and anxiety, this would be the title. I can’t deny that I am struggling. This pregnancy has been tougher on me emotionally. Is it just hormones? Am I stressed out? Why am I like this? I feel out of control of my body and emotions. I am snapping at my kids, lashing out because I get so easily frustrated. Then I feel so guilty and vow to do better. What will they remember about this stage? “Mommy yelled at me a lot” or “mommy cried a lot.” At what point am I doing permanent damage to their fragile souls? I love them so much, but do they even know that? Can they feel that through everything else? I have to make a conscious effort every moment to believe instead that I AM ENOUGH. I have to fight off the lies, the million thoughts on how I could be a better mom, the loud voices that tell me I am failing. It is a struggle that can steal my joy at times, but it is a fight I can win. I am enough, and you are too.

I’ve debated sharing this because it’s a little embarrassing to be vulnerable but I think more of us feel this way than we’d like to admit so here goes. A few months back, someone I know in real life, had regular interactions with, and had been a friend to, unfollowed me out of the blue and basically ignored me when I DM’d her regarding a mutual friend. It bothered me and I was angry and hurt, probably because I’m a chronic people pleaser and couldn’t understand why this person would exclude me among our mutual friends. I felt like there was something wrong with me and started picking myself apart. Let me tell you, your worth is not determined in this app. It isn’t found in how many followers you have, or if you’re in the “in-crowd” of your Instagram circle, or how many likes a photo can get. This experience helped me learn the value of connection. Even on here, I don’t want to treat people and relationships like they are disposable. A follow or interaction means a lot to me because it means you care. I’m not sure what point I’m getting at anymore, but I sense that Instagram isn’t about community the same way it used to be and that’s what is frustrating. This place takes a lot of energy and a lot of our emotional well being gets wrapped up in it whether we want it to or not. So my only challenge to you is to think carefully about the interactions and connections you are making here. There are real people and real feelings attached to these feeds. And on the flip side, don’t let these interactions define you. Know that this place will not fulfill you and only real life experiences and relationships can do that. Peace and love everyone ✌🏻 at the end of it all, we only have each other!

That would explain why he only wants to eat Oreos and ice cream sandwiches lately 🤔 anyone had big life changes with a 3 year old? Do you shield them from what is going on? How do you help them embrace stressful situations? I’ve been trying to keep things as fun and exciting as possible so he sees it as an adventure and not something he is forced in to. But for real I feel like life did not prepare me for this area of parenting AT ALL 😅

I feel guilty admitting this but I kinda miss working. I’m just finishing up what would be my maternity leave, but since we moved, I haven’t found a new job and will be a stay at home mom for a bit. Truthfully, I’m not sure that’s what I want. I feel like that’s “the dream” and what is expected of me. Because why would I want to work when I could stay home with my kids? I worked hard to be a nurse and it just feels weird to embrace a different reality.  I worry I won’t find fulfillment in being a stay at home mom and I don’t think I’d be “good” at it. I think the grass can always seem greener, but we can all agree that being a mom and deciding what is best for ourselves and our family is damn hard.

I cried last night, while fighting the same battle we fight almost every night. Getting Cecilia settled for bed, she won’t take a paci, so she just goes back and forth on me until I can get her to fall asleep and stay asleep. It is the time of day that I want “me” time. A moment alone, time to catch up on housework, a quiet shower. I feel stuck like there’s no end in sight. But I know there is. One day she will settle and sleep without so much rocking and nursing and shushing, and I’ll miss it. The newborn stage is the easiest in some ways and the hardest in others. From one tired mom to another- you can do this and you will get through this 🖤

I got a message a week ago from someone saying I was a horrible mother because all I cared about was Cecilia, and that my boys were acting out because I didn’t love them enough or give them enough attention. First of all, my kids behaved crazy before I had the baby so clearly that person knew nothing 🤷🏻‍♀️ I know what kind of mother I am, but really, we can choose to spread love or hate-it is just that-a choice. This person couldn’t know the road we took to get here. Maybe she’s never struggled with infertility, anxiety, depression, fear, or doubt. She couldn’t know just how hard it is to have one child, let alone 2 or 3. Now I have to learn how to divide my time and attention yet again between another little one who needs me differently but just as much as my other two. There are not enough hands to give them each everything they need in the exact moment they need it. There are not enough eyes to look at all the tiny faces looking up to me all at the same time. One arm holding a baby to breast feed, trying to make lunch and referee fights with the other. Only two legs to carry me back and forth around everywhere tending to this and that as each one needs me. One me. Just one. Serving my children, my husband, my home, and myself. So while there’s not enough of a lot of things, love isn’t one of them. There’s a whole hell of a lot of that, and I choose that. To my friends, to my kids, to myself. Just one big love fest. Because being a mom is hard, being a human is HARD. So choose love.

One of the scariest experiences I’ve had as a mother happened to me today.  It was one of those moments that feels like a movie. Like this can’t be happening to me. My car somehow malfunctioned and long story short locked with both my babies, phone and keys in it. We were in a parking lot and thank god my good friend was there to help. She called 911, who told her there was nothing they could do unless they were in distress and to call a locksmith. My husband is out of town and who knows how long a locksmith would take. As this was happening I coached Ever to try and pull the lock up, but she couldn’t quite reach in her car seat. I told her to unbuckle the top part to get her arms free and to attempt the bottom buckle, but she can never get that one. Somehow she did and I told her through the window to climb to the front seat and unlock the doors. The whole ordeal was probably only 7 minutes, but felt like an eternity. I’ve never been so scared. I’m crying as I type this. You know there are days that just knock you down as a mother. This actually wasn’t one of those days. Despite it being one of the scariest moments of my life. No styled pictures. No fancy photoshoots. I didn't even take my head scarf off until we were getting ready to leave the hospital to go home. None of that mattered, though.

Birthing babies doesn't come easy for me. Ain't nothing about it pretty. I knew that this c-section, my second, was going to be challenging. I packed my favorite, most comfortable nightgown, pulled my hair back, and mentally prepared to go through the grueling physical experience. Even after major surgery, there is no rest for the mama. My #1 priority was getting out of that operating room so I could feed my child. 
This go round, it took nearly 2 hours after my son was born for the doctors to stop my bleeding and get me all stitched up. My husband was with the baby in a holding room, giving him his finger to suck because the nurses wanted to wait as long as possible before giving him formula. They kept telling him, "she should be out shortly" and "just a little while longer, hopefully". Terrence said Jamie was screaming at the top of his tiny lungs at one point, but he still felt confident waiting for me.

I believe that #fedisbest, but I'm grateful that everyone honored my request for my baby's first food to be from me. 
When I finally got to the recovery room, Terrence wheeled Jamie into me and that baby started smacking his lips! He knew his mama...and his milk! He latched on right away, like he had been nursing his entire life.

I was in pain, exhausted, and sore. Even with all of that, when I placed my son to my breast, I felt like superwoman.

Whenever I travel nowadays, I'm so anxious. I beg my husband to follow all of the laws of driving to the tee, and I'm cautious of where we stop. This summer, we went to Oregon on a road trip. As we got further North in California, we started seeing Confederate flags and Trump voter signs and I started to feel super nervous. 
I didn't know what to expect in Oregon. I just wanted to be safe. 
Our first stop when we got into the state was a little breakfast cafe. When we walked in, I saw a sign right in front that said, "We reserve the right to refuse to serve anyone." My heart started beating so hard in my chest, and I was hoping we wouldn't be embarrassed if they chose to turn us away. I held my breath.

When the waitress came up to us with menus, and politely set us at a table, complimented Jamie's hair and asked Ayva how old she was, I finally exhaled.

Different patrons kept coming to our table and asking where we were visiting from, and complimenting us on how well behaved our children were and how adorable they looked. The town "Santa Claus" even stopped by to chat for a few minutes.

Our time in Oregon was lovely. we were the only black people most places we went, but everyone was nice and we had a really good time.

And we were safe. Most importantly, we were safe.

it’s taken me three days to gather my thoughts, these boys will never know how much they help ease the pain.. monday evening i rushed to visit my grandma for what i knew was going to be the last time.. ever.. throughout this past year, weekly i’ve visited her, bringing nixon + sometimes the big boys in hopes to see her light up. she fought hard to stay with us much longer than any of us expected. strong hardly began to define her. she was more than that.. she taught us what family truly stood for. see, she was my grandma but not by blood.. she took me in as hers at 5 years old and for a life time of teachings i’ll forever hold close to my heart. she was beyond special and our connection was something i don’t think i’ll ever experience again. my sons have each been there for me in dark and hard times in which i had no choice but to let the tears roll while continuing to mother them and be the wife to the husband that comes home from long hard days at work. there’s hardly any room to sulk and feel sorry myself. it’s 2am when i’m left alone with my thoughts of past memories that flood and it hurts the most. seeing her merely hours before she left gives me a sort of peace i never thought i would experience after loss. yesterday marked 9 years since loosing my dad.. where i still battle with those emotions. today being my pops’ {grandpa} birthday, my grandma + him finally together again in heaven. being close to family today is where i was meant to be. deciding last minute to cancel our travel plans due to weather, having no clue this in turn would be my last moments with her... no longer in pain, no longer having to fight to be here she is now with our loved ones looking over us. she’s always been an angel to me.. that night driving home after seeing her i felt a moment that i had literally experienced already. a dream.. a deja vu of sorts.. she spoke to me words that i heard before. it hit me like a ton of bricks. i couldn’t control the tears that streamed down my face and the songs that just so happened to play during this time made me an emotional wreck.. that was going to be the last time i would see her and i knew it.. “don’t let me stop you darling”

juggling kids from one thing to another.. ages ranging from a teen down to #ourlittlestwonder ...gaps always scared me, having too many years between one kid to the next.. would they still have a relationship, would they still play, build and create lasting memories of their childhood. gaps weren’t ever happening to me because you see i have one with my sister who’s 12 years younger than i, so this just wasn’t going to happen to me. nope. well yes, in turn, it did. but being where i am now. many years later with 3 boys with gaps i swore never would happen and guess what we can’t always control “life”. “life” has a funny way of sneaking up on you and telling you it’s gonna go this way.. although we create paths our destiny is already paved out for us and little did my heart, mind and soul know that from my eldest to my youngest there would be an exact, by the month even, 12 year gap between my boys. with an almost 8 year gap between my middle and my youngest. i’ve learned and grown so much from these age gaps. each boy had me, only me, before a sibling came.. just in time to start school and for me to dedicate time for my next baby. i’m so proud to have been able to give each child my sole attention. i never knew how much that would mean to me and hope it means something more to them ❤️

This week has been tough for me I mean super T O U G H 😩 honestly probably the toughest week I’ve had since being a mom of three! So many emotions and struggles that literally I sat in my room alone last night and just cried! I debated hardcore on how or even if I should share this but I feel like maybe it could help another mama.... I decided to wean my last baby this past week for good. And since being in the hospital overnight with my gallbladder surgery he was only really nursing(non stop) a night and finally this past Tuesday I had enough I was becoming a binkie I was literally touched out and utterly exhausted 😩 I can not believe how emotional it has me and how my hormones have been so crazy since! But we need to remember to do what is best for us! For each mama and baby! I know a part of me felt guilty the other part sad that I’ll never nurse another baby and even a part of me felt scared for other moms(or anyone really) to judge me. It’s tough sometimes this whole #momlife gig and I think we get so caught up in what we think it is “supposed” to be like and compare ourselves to others so often we forget to just sit back and enjoy the ride! I know my baby is happy, healthy and FED and truly that’s what matters!! #babylincoln #emotionalpost #mylastbaby

I went through complete hell + it made me hard. 
Hard to love God.
Hard to love others. 
Hard to be loved. 
Hard to befriend. 
Hard to be a friend. 
Hard to have as a friend. 
Hard to be compassionate towards and with. 
Hard to have compassion. 
Hard to understand others. 
Hard to be understood. 
Hard to forgive.
Hard to be forgiven. 
Hard to reconcile with others. 
Hard to be reconciled with. 
Hard to forgive others. .... and, I foolishly thought that being hard meant strong. 
That being hard meant more difficult to hurt. 
That being hard meant better. 
That being hard would lead to peace. 
But it led to solitude. 
Hard led to bitterness. 
Hard led to anger. 
Hard led to foolish choices. 
Hard led to more hurt. 
Hard made it a lot easier to be broken. 
Only when I began to soften my heart towards the Lord and allow grace and hope to take root where brokenness, sadness, & disappointment became an expectation, was able to experience what had been lost. 
Love for self. 
Understanding of others. 
Growth and joy. 
Happiness & laughter. 
Peace & a wakefulness that allows me to enjoy every aspect of life. 
Trust, depth, & out of my comfort zone safety in relationships. 
Hope for a future that is more than I ever thought it could be. 
Then, me & my three lived happily ever after. 💕

The past few years have been long....... and, I've endured a lot. A lot that exacerbated some things that I didn't like about myself that came flooding to the surface. I became incredibly impatient, more #anxious and antsy and uncomfortable with new things or when things don't go according to plan or with the unknown, frustrations came easily, & I became even more hard on myself. So moments of high #stress, #tension, #anger, and #sadness were constant.
•
In the midst of all that I began #counseling and a heaviness started to lift from my shoulders. Counseling + personal growth + working hard (HARD!) on forgiveness + letting go of all the things that were preventing me from becoming who I wanted to be. Who I dreamed of being. Who I knew I was deep down at my core.
•
Then, enter Vital Biome. A probiotic that is scientifically proven to reduce all of the feelings I'd been struggling with for years. In tandem with learning how to manage #emotions + #forgive and personal growth that has also opened my eyes a ton, this probiotic has been a total life saver for me. Things that would have set me off and stress me no longer do. I'm able to get through high stress situations (read: mornings) peacefully, patiently, and without losing my sh*t, lashing out, or raising my voice. The peace of my home is proof, the calmness of my kids, and my own demeanor is evidence of a change that has taken place on the inside. From the heart to the gut & I'm so #thankful for #wellness. Emotionally, mentally, & physically I'm becoming a better and better version of myself. The catalyst was beyond painful and hard, but I'm so thankful for it.

This literally doesn’t seem real. The first few months of this pregnancy, I struggled deeply. Unplanned & unwanted 😖. I never imagined adding another kiddo “like this” - before I was married again. There were many seasons in my life where I was a part but didn’t belong. Invited, but not welcomed. Endured, not celebrated. And, just flat out disregarded & dismissed. In response, I secluded. Quit. Disengaged. Stayed quiet. Felt uncomfortable and inadequate. Unworthy and alone.
•
For those experiences I am so incredibly thankful. They taught me how to do my own thing, to not root my value or happiness in the eyes of others, to see rejection as guidance versus a reflection of who I am, and most of trust God wholly.
•
I learned that God is an incredible, satisfying provider and blesses us with unending provision. He gives us good things but more importantly peace. Joy. Friendships. Faith. Belief. A bigger perspective. Opportunities to become what we created us to be. Capabilities. Gifts. Vision. Endurance. A second chance. A place to belong. A place to grow. A way to live a full life of abundance. Love. 
Today, my heart is so full, full to overflowing. I’m grateful everyday, but today that gratitude for every kind of provision spills out of my heart. And, hopefully into the ones around me.
•
I won’t be accepted by most. 
Won’t be good enough for many. 
Will be passed over, ignored, laughed at, and not valued for some reason by someone for the rest of my life.
•
But, I will also be supported, encouraged, loved, emotionally healthy, physically balanced, & loved (again). Room will be made for me. A seat saved with my name on it and surrounded by people who I can give what has been given to me. Over and over and over again. I will seek belonging, unconditional love, value in Christ alone and embrace those he sets in my life who desire the same.
•
This group of ladies is a portion of that. Just a few dreamers and doers and achievers and celebrators and never giving uppers who come from very different places + are along for very different reasons but who are here for the same purpose: to love big + be an example.
•
So thankful that I have been blessed with a place. One I didn’t have to change or pretend or suppress to be a part of. The gratitude is overwhelming.💕

Words to live by ✨ ✨
✨
For years I was stuck in a work environment that I hated. I would wake up dreading going to work, it would give me anxiety, and it even drove me to some of my worst migraines ever. I was new in the field and would always get the heaviest work load — I felt isolated and incompetent. I loved helping my patients, but ultimately, I wasn’t happy. ✨
✨
After a couple of years, I decided it was time to leave. We moved and I found a job that didn’t feel like a “job,” I was finally content. ✨
✨
Looking back, I don’t regret that time. I learned a lot from patients, a few close coworkers and the difference between not wanting to go to work and hating your job. Two completely different things. ✨ ✨
If you’re in the same boat, I hope you can find that truly makes you happy. It make take some trial and error, but in the end, it’s worth it. Don’t be scared to chase your daydream! 💕 #beautywithlily #beautywithlilylifestyle #lifestylebloggers #lubbockblogger #texasblogger #westtexasblogger

“If you tell Amber her shoes are untied, she might start crying.” For as long as I can remember, my intense emotions were joked about in family and friend settings. I used to make them about myself. I now know that it was a defense mechanism. I would keep to myself and retreat to hide my sensitivity. “You’re too sensitive” are words I’ve heard all my life. And they still trigger me to this day. Feeling the depths of every emotion- swimming in sorrow, burning with anger, illuminating with joy - feeling them, being aware of them, NOT suppressing them and accepting them has aided in tremendous healing of my soul. You see, we’re told not to be sad. We’re told not to feel angry. We’re told by everything and everyone around us that we SHOULD be happy. That feeling happy is the goal. That life and the things we share should ‘spark joy’ and that anything that makes us feel sad, hurt, grieved or angry should be tucked away. But can I tell you something? We can hold space for sadness, hurt and anger while we simultaneously hold space for joy, light and positivity. Acknowledging, accepting and learning is vital. Our emotions communicate invaluable insights to us. We can step outside of the narrative and we can burn and rewrite the script. We can be ourselves and we can be enough. We can choose to feel, accept, acknowledge and learn. You’re enough. You’re not weird. And to my fellow empaths, your sensitivity is a gift. A beautiful, valuable and wonderful gift. ♥️ #empaths #deepfeels #emotions #honestmotherhood #reallife #selfdiscovery #everydaymadewell #thoughtsonhealing

Hey, guess what? Marriage is hard. Parenting is hard. We celebrated 7 years of marriage in October and this has by far been the most challenging year we’ve ever faced. So much loss, so much hurt. Healing takes time. Moving forward is almost always slower than we want it to be. But there is no rushing the process. And instead of resisting and fighting, there is so much beauty in ALLOWING and surrendering. NO ONE has their shit together, you guys. Every one is a little bit broken. There are no two journeys alike. Merging DNA, dreams, personalities, backgrounds, histories, traumas, losses, life experiences, triggers, philosophies etc. can be so freaking messy. Throw parenting three tiny humans on top of that AND becoming aware of the healing you need and my my my, messy messy messy. BUT HOLY WOW, this IS IT. This is what we will talk about when our hair shimmers white and our eyes are sunk a little deeper and the lines on our face become more defined. When we look into the faces of our offspring and their offspring and we’ll tell them tales of how we almost didn’t make it BUT WE DID. Because we chose to. And we did the hard as shit work to not just survive BUT TO THRIVE. #thoughtsonhealing #marriage

I once had a boyfriend tell me my ideas about love weren’t realistic. He told me “Love is never like what you see in the movies. You’ll have to lower your expectations if you ever want to be happy.”
•••
A couple of not-so-great breakups later I started seriously doubting that I would ever find someone who I’d genuinely want to share my life with. I thought “What are the chances of finding someone who just ‘gets me’.” When I started to believe finding “the one” wasn’t realistic, I met Chris.
•••
I believe finding each-other at a point in both of our lives where we had already experienced life on our own and knew what we wanted made us appreciate one another even more and realize “this is what I’ve been holding out for”. Sometimes we have to come to know bad to fully appreciate & recognize the good that gets placed in our lives.
•••
I’m not an expert on love but speaking from experience, I believe with all my heart that no one should settle for “just comfortable”.
•••
For those who are still searching
•I know it may feel hopeless at times, but please be patient.
•••
•Hold out for that special person who truly deserves you.
•The one who looks at you like you’re the only person in the room.
•Wait for the one who can make you laugh when you need it most.
•The one who will tell that you they love you each day not out of habit, but because they it crosses their mind so much, they just can’t keep it in.
•••
True love isn’t just a fairytale, but it’s also not always perfect & it shouldn’t be perfect.
•••
Love isn’t always black & white and relationships don’t come in a ‘one size fits all’.
•••
Every relationship has its ups & downs. Any couple who says otherwise isn’t being honest. Every healthy, loving partnership takes work and more importantly the willingness to put in that work.
•••
Your version of love & happiness won’t be the same as the next persons and it shouldn’t be. It just makes finding ‘your person’ even more special and unique since we’re all so different.
•••
In the end, my ex was right, but not in point he was trying to make.
Love isn’t as magical as they show in the movies.
•••
It can be so, so much more.

The other day I was struggling to open a jar of coconut oil and with each attempt I got more and more frustrated. Easton was drawing at the kitchen table and just casually mentions to me “mom why don’t you stop and ask Jesus to help you? You said he can help me make nice choices I bet he can help you! Just say “Jesus can you make me strong enough to open this!” 😭 So of course I did- and it did not work. .

P O S I T I V I T Y 🌿
I’ve had to make some changes to my mindset, in order to rationalise things I can’t control.
⠀⠀
I realised lots of my anxiety was being caused by things that hadn’t even happened yet, things that might never happen and things that could be amazing yet seemed to be so daunting to me.
⠀⠀
I worry all the time that I’m going to hold us back as a family, cause the children to miss out on things and not give them the childhood that they deserve.
⠀⠀
These are obviously really negative thoughts, so to try and prove to myself and push myself to ensure this doesn’t happen we:
⠀⠀
1. Created a memory jar, with the aim to make a scrapbook at the end of the year!

2. Fortnightly date night - taken in turns to arrange - non expensive, from a drink to a meal but us time

3. Book a holiday - majorly out of my comfort zone and something that really scares me but I need to do this one otherwise it’ll hold us back

4. Write down all the good experiences and focus on them

5. Try and live in the now not the next week, month, year as I won’t be this person then

6. Reflect on my amazing achievements in life so far - things that I never thought I could do that I’ve conquered
⠀⠀
Why I am sharing this?
Anxiety can be an extremely lonely place. The most social of Instagram butterflies can feel consumed and depressed by it and no one could know. I know it’s not easy to reach out but I’ve had so many of you do so to me and so if this helps one person I’ll have returned that complete kindness given to me 💕

.
.  In a study of women living in Manchester, UK an estimated 40% of women between the ages of 20-24 were found to be carrying HPV. Unsurprisingly if, like me, you have ever comforted a friend through an STI scare, many of these women reported feelings of shame upon finding out that HPV was a sexually transmitted disease.
“Knowledge that HPV is sexually transmitted was associated with higher levels
of stigma and shame, but not anxiety. Women who knew that HPV is sexually transmitted but not that it is highly prevalent had the highest scores for stigma and shame.”
.
✨
The same study suggested that ‘normalising’ HPV and informing the participants of the study in regard to how common HPV contractions are helped reduce feelings of shame and stigma within these women.
.
⭐️

In the USA only 13 states require sex education to be medically accurate - leaving people young and old in the dark when it comes to developing healthy and informed sexual habits, or removing internalised shame and stigma from their preferences and activities. ⭐️

It’s a constant theme throughout our society that we seek to admire women for their appearance, and at the same time berate them for it. We tell them how to look, how to dress, and what is the flavour of the month in this regard. Those trends have consistently been dictated to us via the male gaze. We are, more often than not, taught to be nothing more than ornamental, and then in turn - in the post feminist era - berated for ‘vanity’ if we do accept the offer of being pinned to a board, and ogled. 
The rush and flux of messages is, ‘look like this, not that, do this, not that’ and more and more, I see other women dictating this, perpetuating a sick culture of body shaming, image shaming, and generally projecting their own issues regarding confidence and insecurity onto the women around them. 
We see less women being lauded for their accomplishments and achievements than we do for their looks, so few online comments across platforms tell women that their ideas are valid and interesting, compared to the running commentary on their natural appearance, visual aesthetic choices and weight. 
It’s incredibly disheartening to think that every obstacle you hurdle over, achievement, or idea you have as a woman will forever be overshadowed with how you looked while doing it. Even in the case of a mistake you made, the argument so often turns to whether the woman in question is attractive enough to garner lenience. 
I am sick of people telling me my value is inherently tied to my appearance, that I am only worth listening to if what I say comes with a hereto-normative patriarchal definition of beauty. If I am palatable enough to be looked at, by men and women alike, only then can I be listened to. That’s not the world I want to live in. It’s not the culture I want to promote. 💙 .

A few years ago I lost a shit tonne of weight. I didn’t do it in a particularly healthy manner either. I won’t give specifics but it wasn’t worth it. I talk a lot about body image these days, and that’s because mine has improved like hell since then. When I was 21-23 I was so thin I could lay on my side & my thighs wouldn’t fall to touch. Everywhere I went men and women would compliment me, saying I looked ‘amazing’ or ‘like a little doll’. The thing was, I spent so much time as a teenager trying to be thinner & have a flat stomach rather than just accept that I’m a short, curvy little Australian girl. When it finally happened this slimness did not make me happier. Despite my body image issues, I had always felt attractive to myself - no matter my weight I LIKED myself, and as a teen I just accepted, ‘cool I’m not attractive - but I like how I look so that’s fine’. What changed when I dropped down below what I think of as my ‘normal healthy’ weight, was that I felt MORE insecure than ever before - because no one had ever complimented me this much before. I started attaching any semblance of aesthetic worth to being a certain size & that exterior motivation. It was extremely egoistic and extremely strange to experience. 
Luckily I gained it back, and with it I gained back a sense of self worth outside of of my appearance. I realised that my natural size is nothing to be ashamed of. Nor is some cellulite, or having to go up a dress size when trying on clothing. My body has always fit into a ‘straight size’ standard, and I’m a very petite person anyway, so it’s insane to me how much pressure is placed on women of a small to average dress size to be EVEN smaller, thinner, prettier, better in every conceivable way - and then again ridiculed at any point that they may deviate from that standard. While also being told to ‘be naturally beautiful’. It’s insanity. 🌈✨

I hate to be the bearer of some #realshit because most people can’t handle it. If things aren’t going too good in your life or a ship (relationship, friendship, work ship, etc.) you ARE part of the problem. No one is ever an innocent bystander there is always something that you could have done differently to get a better outcome. Let’s re-route our thought processes and get to the core of our main issues. Take responsibility for your involvement,  stop playing the blame game, being bullheaded,  quit being selfish, and truly do some self evaluation. I never wanted to grow up. Never wanted to drive, get married, have a house, have kids, or otherwise be tied down to anything that felt like responsibility. I knew these things wouldn’t be options for me anyway, and worried I would fail at them if they were presented to me. I wanted to be free to do what I wanted and go where I pleased. I even got a Peter Pan tattoo to remind me— never grow up.
.
But another phrase from the Peter Pan film eventually began haunting me. “To live would be an awfully big adventure.” Living without ties to others started to become boring, and quickly felt meaningless. I loved my friends and fleeting romances, but what else was there in this life? What could “living” really mean?
.
Though my life was full of fun, I was not truly known— by others or myself. I hadn’t plumbed the depths of love I was capable of. I didn’t know how patient I could be, or how impatient. I didn’t know how deeply I could feel for others, or how profoundly others could hurt me.
.
To live would be an awfully big adventure. And I do love an adventure.
.

Our beloved Riley has struggles with regulating his emotions and behaving in appropriate ways. We are often called to pick him up because he has acted out in school (swearing at other kids, throwing things, refusing to do what the teacher asks). We get texts and emails about his behavior and how disruptive it is in class. We’ve tried changing his diet and getting him more exercise (he does two hours of parkour three days a week). We’ve tried sticker charts and screen time as a reward. We’ve tried grounding him as a punishment. We go to therapy with him, he has an IEP, we meet with the school staff. Nothing has truly helped him.
.
Then this week, he began taking medication. Combined with our other in-school and at-home supports, he is a completely different kid. It’s as if the ugly voice in his head that tells him he’s not Enough is just... gone.
.
I am really sad that parents are shamed for trying medical intervention to help their kids. We take Tylenol for headaches and put bandaids on our wounds. But somehow if a wound is chemical, it isn’t seen as valid and we are expected to treat it differently. I am so proud that we’ve loved Riley through all his struggles. But he deserves a shot at life without the scary voice that points out all the negatives around him. I’m not gonna lie— it’s hard to use your voice to speak up, even when the stakes are low. Last week at the gym, I heard a personal trainer say something to a client that I thought was inappropriate. I mulled it over for days to see if I might be overthinking it. Every time I went to the gym, I would imagine going to a staff member or a manager to let them know what I had heard. And every day... I didn’t do it.
.
There have been so many times when I have brought something troubling to a person in a position of power and had it dismissed... or worse. I’ve been belittled and berated in the past for pointing out issues of racism, sexism, transphobia, you name it. I really love my gym and don’t want to burn any bridges there. And at the same time, if someone like me who has male-passing privilege doesn’t bring up issues of sexism… who will? Finally, I promised myself that if I saw the one visibly-queer staff member at the gym again, I would pull her aside and tell her what I heard.
.
Today I rehearsed what I would say over and over again. I literally practiced it out loud, I was so nervous. And then when I got to the gym today, she was there and I knew I had to tell her. She sat down with me and I explained what I had heard, and her face registered shock. She thanked me for bringing it to her, let me know that she would take care of it right away, and reiterated that yes, that was an inappropriate thing for him to have said and I was right to bring it to her.
.
I am so ashamed that it took me days and days to bring up a very simple matter of one inappropriate comment overheard by a stranger at the gym. But it reminds me of all the systems in place to keep us from talking. All the memories of dismissal, all the cultural messages to not be so sensitive, to not take things so seriously.
.
We have to push against them every single day. Especially when we have privilege in the situation. Resist, resist, resist.

The first time I got pregnant it was on accident.

I mean, I had stopped taking my hormones and was intending to get pregnant EVENTUALLY. But before I knew my body was ready, it happened. Biff and I were definitely NOT ready. We thought we would have months to prepare and then suddenly it was here. But then just as suddenly it was gone. There was an ultrasound appointment with no heartbeat and then there was so much blood and then… I wasn’t pregnant anymore.

1 in 4 known pregnancies ends in miscarriage. I was reassured over and over again that I didn’t do anything wrong and this could happen to anyone. None of their assurances really broke through my stunned state. I wanted a baby but I wasn’t ready for a baby yet and then I wasn’t having a baby after all.

Miscarriage is shockingly messy. I tried to hide its messiness from Biff because I was terrified he would get spooked and decide we shouldn’t have a baby after all. So I was left alone to deal with this feeling that my body had betrayed me. Like it had failed. As a trans person, I already had a complicated relationship with my body. I have loved its competence but I have not loved the way the world has viewed it; the gaze of strangers has marred my own view of my body forever.

Near the end of the miscarriage, I called my provider’s office in tears and talked to a nurse who tried to calm me down. When I was ready, she said, it would be important for me to find gratitude for my body. A miscarriage isn’t a failure, she told me. It’s a success. My body knew that this pregnancy wasn’t viable and my body took care of it so I would be healthy for the next pregnancy. My body took care of me.

I’d never really thought about all the things my body does for me, but in that moment I did. Breathing and eating and carrying me through this life. And then, when I needed it most, it protected me so that one day I could have a baby. My body had succeeded. It had taken care of me. And 6 months later, I did get pregnant and I have a baby.

And I am profoundly grateful.

One year ago today, I took this horrible selfie as 700 students flooded into the auditorium of Lake Oswego High School. I was terrified.

High school wasn’t great for me. And it was only partially the fault of my peers. Mostly I didn’t know who I was so I awkwardly tried to blaze my own trail, unclear of exactly where I was supposedly going. I was smart but not studious, hard-working but not disciplined, theatrical but not interesting. Life hadn’t really HAPPENED to me yet, but I was convinced it had.
.
And yes, there was bullying. Insults and name-calling and physical stuff. So my heart sped up when I saw those students file into their seats, skeptically awaiting my training on trans issues. It ended up being one of the most harrowing presentation experiences of my life.
.
But not because they were cruel— because they were bold. One student proclaimed that they had always felt trapped in the wrong body and have often begged their parents to help them change genders... and did I think they were trans? Another asked me, in front of the whole student body, whether I’d had “the surgery.” Cringe-worthy, for sure. But also bold. Honest. True.
.
And I’d rather deal with a hundred teenagers asking me to diagnose them as trans in front of their school (and a thousand students asking me about my transition) than just one adult saying they feel sorry for my children because they’re being raised in a queer household. The messy openness of youth is manageable. The bigotry of adults is not.
.

I worry about social media and what it’s doing to people who want to be parents or who are already parenting. I worry that the most touching, sweet moments are lifted up as the norm while the hard, gut-wrenching moments are brushed aside or retouched into a tidy teachable moment.
.
I hear from a lot of young people telling me I’ve inspired them to imagine parenthood, and I’m proud of that. But even though it makes me feel like an old man, I want to tell them to WAIT. Please, have all the babies you want. Adopt, co-parent, birth, surrogate, donate, however you want to build a family... do it. But do it when you’re ready. Being a parent isn’t all cuddles and “I love you” and high-fiving each other for a job well done. Leo hasn’t been happy in days. He’s hit the terrible two’s and just hates everything. Riley has started telling me, to my face, that he thinks it’s weird to have a dad that gave birth. Tonight alone, Hailey has asked me 8 times if she can have her tablet and when I said no she started screaming at me. I’ve been putting a lot of energy into a fun little weekend for us in Seattle so we can be together with a hot tub and some time that isn’t about my surgery or the house being clean. Riley is straight-up refusing to go. “It sounds boring! Leo might make a noise in the car! I hate art museums! That hotel looks stupid!”
.
The hard parts of parenting aren’t even what you think they will be. When prospective parents talk about diapers and no sleep, I want to laugh. If only the hardest parts were diapers and no sleep!!! Feeling like a failure, like they don’t love you, like someone else would be better than you are, like the time is flying and they’ll only remember the worst parts, like they’re your own personal bully from high school LIVING IN YOUR HOUSE, like you’re parenting Eeyore and nothing you do will ever be good enough, like the teachers wonder if you’re even trying at home, like you’ll never have enough money to catch up... that’s the hard stuff. It is not for the faint of heart. Make sure you have your shit together as much as possible. You’re going to need everything you’ve got to give those tiny humans what they deserve. Which is everything.

When I first started transitioning I was terrified. I wasn’t very masculine and lots of people told me I would never look like “a real man.” But more importantly, I knew that taking testosterone would mean that I would never be “normal” again. I was crossing an invisible barrier that I could never come back from.
.
Why be happy when you can be normal?
.
I feel like I’m supposed to say I was only elated to transition, and that was part of it— of course. But I was also profoundly sad. I was letting go of my chance to have a normal life. To find love and get married and have kids and get a job and just be a regular person. I could have done it. It would have been a lie and I would have been miserable, but I could have done it. I’m a good actor. Instead I chose a life where I would always be in between— caught between worlds. No straight man would want me, because I would look like a man. And what gay man would want me, considering how different my body would be, compared to other gay men? It was like strapping on a backpack and heading into the unknown.
.
Here there be dragons.
.
Having top surgery is a similar process of unfolding conflicting emotions. Though I love my life and who I’ve become, the pull to be normal is strong. I’ve crossed a hundred barriers since that first shot in 2002, but every one of them felt insurmountable at the time. If I have surgery, am I once more letting go of any chance to be “normal”? Normalcy is a hell of a drug, and it still tempts me from the periphery... even though I know I’m better off without it.
.

I once spent an entire year learning how to be open to criticism. Up until that year, I was a really defensive person, which made it hard to be my boss, colleague, or partner. Anything even remotely critical felt like an attack to me, and instead of listening for what was true, managing my own response, and integrating the feedback into my day-to-day, I would just attack the person who tried to tell me what I should be doing differently.

During that year when I decided to fix this problem, I put a LOT of work into figuring out why I was so defensive and how I could be different. One hack I learned is a simple phrase: “I can see that.” If Biff tells me I don’t clean enough around the house, rather than listing off everything I’ve done that day, I try to take a breath and say, “I can see that.” It’s how I’m able to trick my brain into actually trying to see the situation from his perspective. When my boss tells me I missed a deadline or should have communicated better about a change in a project... “I can see that.” If Riley tells me he feels it’s unfair that he loses screen time after a rough day at school, I respond, “I can see that.” The magic about this phrase is that it’s neither agreeing nor disagreeing— it’s getting me on the same page as the person I’m speaking with. It’s getting me out of a headspace where I’m viewing us as opposing forces, and into the headspace where it’s not me versus them, it’s me AND them versus the problem.

I still feel defensive when someone points out a flaw in my reasoning or actions, or calls me into account for not being impeccable with my word. But after a full year of working on the skill, I have so many more tools to help me handle these conversations with ease and even joy. Feel free to steal this tip and use it in your own life! And tell me— how do you check your own ego, get out of your own way, and take in feedback (even when it’s painful)?

I sat him down and we worked on reframing our inside voice so we don’t fall into common traps: “I’ll never get my privileges back” becomes “It will be hard to get my privileges back.” “Dada will be mad at me” becomes “Dada loves me all the time, even when he’s mad at me.” We walk through expectations and consequences and reminders of how much we love him.

They never tell you how much parenthood feels like failing. But each day you get up and promise to do better than the last. ❤️❤️❤️

Last week, I noticed that a boutique in Portland was selling a tote bag that said “trans lives matter.” It made me really angry. The founders of the Black Lives Matter movement have asked other movements to please not co-opt their phrase. “Black Lives Matter” was created explicitly to lift up violence against black people, and so many things created to serve black folks get stolen and rebranded in ways that don’t end up helping them. So leaders in other movements have agreed not to say “___ lives matter.” Seeing it in a window of a cutesy shop really upset me, and I’ve been mentally writing a call-out blog post about how and why this shouldn’t have happened.
.
Today I found myself walking by that same shop, and I went in to take a photo of the bag to accompany the scathing post I’d been drafting in my head. There weren’t any out so I asked the lady if she had any in the back. She didn’t. We got to talking, though, and she mentioned she was the buyer for the store. I took a risk and confessed that I wasn’t there to buy the tote— I was there to take a photo so I could call her out for selling the bag. I explained why the phrase could be considered disrespectful to the revolutionary work done by @blklivesmatter, and she was appalled.
.
“I had no idea, and that makes total sense. I just won’t sell that bag anymore.” And that was it. I didn’t have to organize a picket or write a call-out post or shame them publicly. I just had to have a human conversation about how the impact of an action was different from the intent... and the problem got fixed.
.
I was terrified to talk to her directly. So terrified that I hadn’t even considered it as a tactic! They say when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail. I have to remember that I have more tools in my toolbox... and I don’t always need to use my hammer.
.
(Photo from 2008, when anger was the primary driving force behind my activism. There is anger in me still, as there always will be. But it now stands alongside hope, love, and acceptance— acceptance that my way is not the only way, that my ideas are not the right ideas ((they’re just mine))... that I cannot fix everything.)

Two years ago, my regular clothes stopped fitting me. As I outgrew my favorite shirts and pants, I reluctantly embraced my visibility as a pregnant man. People were confused about why I would tell my story publicly. I’m an invisible trans person— it’s a small, awkward club. I blend in with everyone else and am not subjected to transphobia on a daily basis (unless I have to interact with health care providers, the police or other legal entities, academic institutions, the government, TSA, or anyone else who may care about my body or legal gender status). If I have been handed this privilege of being able to slide by under the radar, why would I choose to be visibly trans?!
.
At first, I thought no one would notice. I’m small, so I was hoping my belly might be small and easy to hide. The opposite happened. It became really obvious what was going on—I was a pregnant man. And while some people thought it was a miracle of modern medicine, most people were able to deduce that I must be transgender, and I became visibly trans for the first time in decades. Everyone who saw me knew— that’s a transgender person. And I faced what every visible trans person faces. Disgust, vitriol, violence, negative and hateful trolling, day after day after day. It was an experience I wouldn’t wish on my worst enemy, but now that I’m on the other side of it I am grateful for how much it taught me. I stepped into the shoes of those who cannot choose who knows they are trans, and I learned first-hand what that was like. My commitment to eradicate transphobia deepened even further. I mean, I always  KNEW transphobia existed— of course I did. Trans people are most likely to die as a result of hate crimes. Trans people are four times more likely to live on less than $10k a year. I’ve lost friends to transphobic violence. But I didn’t know in my body what it’s like to trigger a reptile-brain response from strangers, just by virtue of existing. I didn’t know truly how vicious strangers could possibly be.
.
There is great beauty in the world, and there is great suffering. If you don’t suffer, find a way to empathize with those who do and use that as fuel for your fire.

#tbt 3 months ago, I was diagnosed with bells palsy. I was ashamed of my face. It almost stopped me from attending a close friend's graduation party. I remember the knots in my stomach when they wanted to take pictures. I didn't know how to smile & I was incredibly self conscious. I tried to focus on the kids & my hubby & I. Our friends are Nigerian, so we wore the African shirts they brought us back from home.
At the party, no one said a word about my face or looked at me funny. My friend just hugged me & thanked me for coming. 
Fast forward to today & I still feel like I have a film over my right eye. I had to get a new prescription, but for the most part you can't tell I still have Bells Palsy. This experience has taught me so much about compassion, physical deformities, grace & compassion. I'm thankful that my face is back to normal, but for some people this is their normal. I watched Wonder today & cried. I made my 4 & 7 year old watch with me. We talked about differences & how we approach people with disabilities. I also threatened their lives if I ever heard them making fun of someone because of how they look. 
They say what doesn't kill you makes you stronger. It does if you choose to make yourself stronger. It's easy to feel self pity when life doesn't happen the way we expect it to. But our attitude can truly change the trajectory of our future. So today, choose to see the glass half full. And if you are in a season of pain, know that grieving does not equal weakness.

A few posts back, I mentioned it being almost a year since we announced we were having another baby. When we first found out, I freaked out. I actually cried tears of fear not joy. It had only been 4 months post partum since Amelia was born, and there I was about to go through the waves of pregnancy all over again. About to have 3 kids, 3 and under.
.
And the pregnancy was not any better this third time around. Everything that could go wrong, felt like it did. Alyssa was measuring small (Amelia did too. Induced with her little over 2 weeks early because she stopped growing, so I feared the same for Alyssa). I also found out at my 20 week ultrasound, I had complete placenta previa — where my placenta was covering my cervix completely.
.
I mentally prepared myself for the outcome of Alyssa coming possibly early. At 30 weeks, my placenta had not moved, so it was certain I’d be scheduled for cesarean and certain I’d have bleeds. For the remainder of my pregnancy, I was on edge. My husband and I made plans on who we’d call first, who’d come to watch the girls, etc. but when it happened — my first and only hemorrhage — we were still in shock. How does one mentally prepare for that?
.
34 weeks and 3 days early. It was a blur coming out of major surgery. I wasn’t even aware she was sent straight to the NICU. I saw her for a minute after she was born. It was almost 30 hours before I saw and held her. I don’t know how to explain what I felt when I saw her thereafter — she had the CPAP on covering her puffy little face, and wires everywhere. I felt love, but also fear; tearsof joy and fear welling up. She spent 34 days in NICU. Any parent of a baby in NICU knows, the moment all wires were finally off and I could see her face clearly — without wires, feeding tube —is how I still feel when I see that sweet face of hers. I just want to cry tears of complete happiness every time.
.
We are SO lucky & blessed to have her. Things happen for a reason, and she is ours. She’s our little warrior, our sweet peanut, our surprise miracle preemie baby. ❤️ Alyssa completes us.
.
.
.
.
.
.

This throwback photo of me and Ava is reflective on how I feel since yesterday’s news of the mass shooting in Florida. I want to pick my children up and runaway to a remote island and shelter them from the world. It’s a sad reality that since this year, there have been 18 school shootings around the United States. Let’s not count how many there have been the past 19 years since Columbine.
.
Schools should be a safe haven. A parent should be able to send his/her kid off and not have to think about if it’ll be the last time they see their child. A young child (especially in pre-K) shouldn’t have to practice “if a person shows up with a gun” drill.
.
When Columbine happened in 1999, it became my fear as I entered high school. I witnessed bullying going on, I was bullied myself a few times in junior high, and I feared someone would retaliate and show up with a gun adding our school into history. Now that I am a parent, I’m petrified of Ava and my girls going to school. Fears of being bullied or even being a bully herself. So what can we do? Yes we can vote for stricter gun laws, yes we can vote for change to happen, but change starts at home. As parents, we are our children’s world. They are sponges and they’re learning how to act, how to speak, how to think from us — it’s up to us to guide them. My husband and I are raising our girls to be strong and kind and brave and teach kindness to others. To stand up for themselves and for others, and speak out on anything they feel and see isn’t right. Our children today are our world’s future, and it’s up to us to make sure there is even a future for them. #teachkindness #honestmotherhood

#Threenager: First they’re sour.. then they’re sweet.
.
No one told me that Ava would go from being 2 years old to 13 overnight. Clearly this threenager of mine with her sass, her erratic emotions, her mood swings, her fight for independence is going to be the death of me. She’s so stubborn and snotty it baffles me. She will go from loving waffles to hating them and wanting only cereal then wanting waffles again after said meltdown of me giving her cereal all in one morning. She will insist on picking out her own clothes and when she puts her shoes on the wrong foot and I try to help her to correct it, she’ll give me this look as if to say, “I MEANT to do that.”
.
Then as if a light switch went off, she can be the sweetest toddler there is and I wish she’d stay this little forever. She loves to cuddle, she will come up behind me and give me the biggest hugs, she is so sweet with her sister. She always wants to be around us and when she wants just mommy, it makes my heart melt because it’s at that moment I am her favorite person. She’ll tell me how pretty I look when I am (rare-moon) getting ready which is a nice change from her, “no, mommy is not pretty. AVA, is pretty.” (😳 Say whaaaat?! Cue Stephanie Tanner’s voice, “how rude!”)
.
Gosh, this age.. these years.. are going to go by so fast and as crazy and embarrassing as her meltdowns can be, I cry at the thought of her truly growing up and not wanting to even be in the same vicinity as her father and I. So may we embrace this threenager and guide her to be not so much of a rambunctious teenager when she really is one, and may we have the patience to go through these threenage years again.. 2 more times. 🙈

We’ve all had those days... the days that come to an end and you don’t know whether to cry because it’s been the hardest, longest day or sink into a subtle happiness because the day is finally over. Those days have been coming more often lately and I haven’t been able to pinpoint where this feeling of nothingness is coming from, that’s honestly the best way I can explain it... nothingness. It’s not happy, it’s not sad, it’s not angry or calm, it’s empty. After the kids go to sleep I find myself self reflecting and it’s not always in the best light • yes anxiety will do this to a person, no matter how perfect their life may seem on the superficial side • looking back at regrets for things I didn’t get to do with the kids that day, or falling into a depression because it feels like everything in my life is changing uncontrollably and I just want it to pause for a moment until I can catch my breath. Along with the thoughts of everything I desire in life seeming so far out of reach, discouraged is where I’ve found myself. Everyone has these days and it’s okay. I’m not asking for help, or pity, I just want others going through this same feeling of nothingness to know they are not alone and no matter how perfect an instagram feed may look, the person in those squares has struggles of their own that they don’t always share. Tomorrow is a new day and as long as we remember to breathe, it has the potential to be beautiful.
.
.
Breathing • I have anxiety to the fullest, my attacks come when I’m not even thinking about anything or stressed out at that time - they just happen but I have realized lately that the more I breathe, the less attacks I have. Take 1 minute, every hour or two to focus on your breathing. Breathe until you feel it in the very bottom of your stomach & then slowly exhale, think of calming thoughts as you do this. I know it sounds cliche but it’s something that I’ve found helps me stay relaxed. As always, my dms are open to you all for anything you may need to talk about, you don’t have to carry all the weight on your own 🌿

How do you hold onto power without swinging to extremes? On one side we're in danger of giving our power away, letting others make decisions for us, allowing their opinions to shake us around until we don't recognize our lives anymore; laying down our needs like they don't matter as much as their's. ON THE OTHER HAND: We can crush the people around us with our power by dominating or disregarding what is important to them and only serving our own purpose and wants and needs. How do you find a middle ground without dominating other's? 🌚🖤Pay attention to where you leak power. Notice the people, places, and circumstances that suck your power away. 🌚🖤when going into those spaces or being around those people, have some kind of plan or resolve ahead of time to stand your ground. There is so much miscommunication and misunderstanding that can happen this can be a terrifying topic to have with friends, family, etc... there is such a potential to be misunderstood, judged or abandoned. It's scary because you want a deep and meaningful connection so bad with someone that sometimes you think you would be willing to neglect your own needs in favor of keeping everyone else happy with you. It's scary, but it's important because sustainable relationships happen when everyone is honest about what they want. It's also important for the simple fact that HELLO, THIS IS YOUR LIFE- NO ONE ELSE'S.✨
When a good girl's gone bad, she's gone forever; I hope you mourn forever 🎈

For all the parents out there making lunches, putting anxious kids to bed, and running through the tasks you didn't accomplish this weekend (even though you fully intended to) Ace and I feel you. Sunday nights are hard. Be strong. Snuggle fierce!

It's #thankfultuesday. I'm NOT thankful that Ace got sick again this weekend and that we've had to cancel his surgery for the second time in a row. I'm also NOT thankful that he lost a lens on his glasses (for the 4th time since September!) and that he is once again living without clear vision.

But there are reasons to be thankful today. For one, the antibiotic from last week is still in Ace's system. Which means that this particular virus should not turn into an ear infection. I'm also thankful for how our Christmas tree makes sick days much more beautiful. And thankful that even though Ace is a three year old he still sleeps and snuggles with his little butt up in the air. And thankful for all the doctors trying to find a way to schedule the surgery again. And I'm thankful for our insurance. (So so thankful for insurance. Peace and prayers for all of those not as lucky.) What about you?  What are you thankful for, friends?

#acefaceismyfriend #theluckyfew

It can be so hard to talk to our kids about race. But here's the deal: When we have a president who lives his life according to the values of the Empire (a world in which only the strongest, smartest, rich, beautiful and successful have worth), when the leader of our country disparages entire countries and peoples as worse than trash? That's when every one of us has to learn to speak out. Whether we feel up to the task or not.

Because to fight for Ace's value in this world also means to fight for the value of every Dreamer here illegally, every child of color in our country, every baby and mama in Haiti or in the beautiful and distinct cultures and communities of Africa.

Because, thank God, the president and his words have a lot less power than an army of fierce mamas who teach our children to love, to shout the value of the marginalized and pushed aside, to demand that our country become a place where no person, regardless of race, legal status, orientation, or disability is crushed by the powerful.

Let's raise our voices loud. (PS Here's a book I've loved reading with my kids. The story of God's work in and through African Americans in the US, as told through the beatitudes.) #shouttheirworth #theluckyfew #acefaceismyfriend #loveanyway

As I listened to the hearing yesterday, I couldn't help but think of my sisters out there (1 in 3 of the women who follow this Instagram feed, statistics tell us) who have suffered deeply because of sexual assault. To every one of you, I'm so sorry for what you've carried this week.

Listen, I can't authentically champion the rights and value of my son and other people with different abilities and not speak up when there is injustice for other groups undervalued in our society. 
Jesus taught me that the greatest blessings are for the weak, the ones who seek justice, the ones who go unnoticed by the people in power. When a woman's  story of assault is disregarded, written off, or explained away, those of us with voices are called to stand on the side of the powerless. 
So I'll stand on the side of our babies who are born with differences, and I'll stand on the side of the women who are disbelieved. And I'll stand on the side of my brothers and sisters of color who daily live in a society that was built on a system that pushes them down instead of pulling them up.

And that's where the blessings will always be, friends. My man Jesus said so in the Sermon on the Mount. The good life is right there beside the weak, the oppressed, and the marginalized. 
Here's a picture of my little boy, who may be written off by many because of his diagnosis at birth. But we're not writing him off, right? He will do amazing things. And just as we see his value, we can see the value of one another. We can listen to each other. We can learn. We can stand beside the women who need us to hear them, believe them.

#fridaysermon #notpoliticshumanity #shouttheirworth #listentowomen

After moving out, separating, and being on my own, I always thought “well I guess I’ll just be single for the rest of my life, because who’s going to want to be with me? Someone with three kids? Then fast forward to when I first made my Match.com account...I made it for the hell of it. For shits and giggles. Looking back I’m like why did I even make it in the first place? I honestly expected nothing from it. I didn’t even have it for a week, didn’t respond or talk to anyone, and was just going to delete it. The day I was going to delete it, I got a message from Frank. Why I messaged him back? I have no idea other than I think throughout our lives we have moments where our intuition tells us when something is right or wrong. Something told me to message him back and it has felt right every. single. day since then. I can’t tell you how lucky I feel every day that I met someone who loves me for me, as well as the kids. Sure, he isn’t their biological father and never will be, but the fact that they adore and love him so much is something I couldn’t have asked more of. Of course, things aren’t this huge fairytale where everything is flawless and perfect. There has been ups and downs, disagreements, unexpectedness, but since day one my kids and I have never been treated like baggage or something he would have to accept. We weren’t a burden, but instead a bonus.

What started as just a simple runny nose and low grade fever in the afternoon, turned into a 107 temperature and race to the emergency room at midnight.

There are a lot of things I could say about everything that happened- but the biggest thing that stands out in my memory is this: As I stood there watching drs and nurses work and work and work to revive my baby- I thought to myself- this is actually happening. I am living my worst nightmare. I’m not going to get to take him home. And I was a mess. I was not strong. I was not composed. I was not even there for him because I couldn’t even comprehend where I was and what was happening. It has completely ripped me apart and destroyed a sacred part of my mothering- that part where you like to think it will never happen to you.

They admitted us for monitoring and IV medication and they couldn’t get an IV in his precious little body and his painful screaming makes me weep as it still rings in my ears.

It was truly the worst night of my life. Seeing this close to how everything could have been destroyed- watching and feeling my heart break into a million tiny pieces- and yet, he is okay. HE IS OKAY 😭😭 Finn was smiling, waving, and passing out high fives this morning like nothing had ever even happened. And I’m so grateful.

A few words that describe me: analytical, highly risk averse, skeptical. I don’t like to do things unless I know that I can be good at them. I don’t like the feelings of embarrassment, exposure, or the odds not being in my favor. In the past, I have chosen to not pursue, try, or tell people about certain things for fear of looking stupid, messing up, or straight up failing.

But this time? I’ve decided to just GET OVER IT. Forget my M.O. Forget my insecurities and doubt and “logic”. I’m doing what I want and refusing to fear the risk of failure.

I have finally found a product line that I love and am completely obsessed with. I have wanted this for my family for ages but have been too afraid to just DO IT. And now that I have? The scared part of me wants to just be all hush hush and never say anything about it at all. But I’ve decided I don’t want to live my life as a cynic- a skeptic anymore. So, this new business? It’s just one giant step for me to overcoming that.

So cheers to an optimistic, goal setting, big dreaming, Mom boss Courtney.

Two years ago we were together in Destin and we weren’t sure that we were going to stay married. Or, at least, I was pretty sure we wouldn’t. After the hardest summer of our lives, I was so tired and heartsick and just not really sure I was ready to put in all of the work it was going to take to survive us.

But, somehow, by God’s grace alone- we chose to work really freaking hard to change where we were, who we were, and where we were going.

Initially, we met with our pastor every single week (he called it “triage”) Then, we moved on to regular marriage counseling a few times a month for a full year (then we had a third baby and life went bonkers)

And now, here we are- two years later, back in Destin- better and stronger than ever. Not perfect. Not by any means. But so different. Completely changed (changing?) and so thankful for our commitment to each other that saved us.

This is hard for me to write about but I figure if I feel compelled to write it, it’s because God has placed it on my heart to share with you because someone needs to hear it. So if you do, I want you to know this: if you are in a marriage that you feel like isn’t going to survive, it can. It will be hell to fix. Honestly, it will probably be the hardest thing you’ll ever do. But you can do it. You don’t have to live in the same place you are today. Get help. Change yourself. He will change too. Change together and work so freaking hard to get to a place where it was all worth it. You can do it. Even if you feel like you can’t.

Ugh guys, Sorry for not giving an update. I was hoping she would get better by now and I could update with that. I didn’t mean to worry anyone. Ivy is ok, She is SO happy and acting almost like her normal self but her internals don’t match that. We are still doing her air trials every day-twice a day but we are now switching them to only once a day because they don’t want to push her too hard and she is failing all of them quite badly. Her heart rate goes up and her oxygen levels go way down so she just isn’t ready yet. She is fighting off three viruses so her body needs time. With that being said there is a light at the end of the tunnel, If she fails the next air trial then we will be hooking her up to a machine tomorrow night to approve her for home oxygen and we will be hopefully going home on Friday if all the stars align. I am praying that her levels will rise and she won’t need home oxygen but right now it’s just a waiting game (A really terrible one) but we are hanging in there as best as we can. Tonight is our 8th night here and I am desperately missing home, My girls (They are now sick so we are trying to keep them away from Ivy just incase which leaves very little time for me to spend with them and it’s killing me) anyways I’m just feeling quite numb to all it all maybe that’s why I’ve been so quiet. I’m just drained, Physically & emotionally. I just want to go home and so does my sweet girl. #ivyrose

Defeat is the best way to describe how I feel. I don’t want to come on here and complain or have a pity party but this is just my truth. They try to to take Ivy off oxygen two times a day, Everyday. Once in the middle of the night and once during the day...Still no changes, Honestly barely any progress. Day after day of anticipation knowing that she needs to be off oxygen for one full sleep in order for us to go home and then we take her off and watch her levels drop low and then knowing right then and there that we are here for atleast one more night. Again. One more night away from my other babies and husband, One more night of anxiousness and worry. Tonight will be our sixth night here and Im trying to stay positive and tell myself that this is just a short time of our lives and it will pass but it’s just hard. Really really hard. I just want my baby better, So so badly. 💔

Just when I thought I was drained life hits harder. If you’ve been following my stories then you know my sweet angel has RSV. We are admitted to the hospital and hopefully only have one more night here but we will see how she does tonight and what the doctor says in the morning. We are missing the girls SO much and this is so hard on all of us but we are in such good hands and the docs and nurses have been nothing short of amazing. Poor Paytee had a breakdown last night so my Dad drove her down to us super late so she could say hi (So thankful for my family). Poor Cal was so confused and so sad to see her bestfriend like this today, She started to cry and kept saying Ivy owies. My heart broke. Then Ivy gave the biggest smile when she heard her sister and daddy’s voice and my heart felt so whole again. I’ve been thinking so much about all of you Mom’s and Dad’s who have been in this situation or worse and my heart is just broken for you. If you are or have gone through your child being hospitalized then I am sending you an immense amount of love and hugs because this is so incredibly hard. Thank you all SO much for your love and prayers. 
P.S-Also can I just say how amazing a mother’s touch is? She literally has barley let me leave her to have a sip of water or even go pee but that is ok with me because she needs me more than ever and I need her even more. #ivyrose 💗

Motherhood has stretched me emotionally, spiritually, mentally, and well physically 😂 I remember after having Harper I hardly recognized who I was. Hair a mess, tears on my cheeks, belly sagging, shirt stained with who knows what, bags under my eyes darker than black coffee, emotions running wild, little hope, and crippling anxiety. I had a moment where I thought to myself “is parenting growth or just plain torture?” I’ll tell you most days it felt like the latter 🙈 Literally collapsing on the floor & falling asleep from pure exhaustion. Since preparing for this second baby, I have to tell you how grateful I am for all those “torturous” moments. I look at my round pregnant self in the mirror & I love who I am. I am stronger, smarter, more patient, driven, grateful, humble than I have ever been because of raising my tiny girl. Yesterday the power went out in our apartment for almost 12 hours. Our entire apartment runs on electricity. No hot water. No heaters. No dishwasher. No tv. No light. No phone charger. No microwave. No stove. No oven. No pretty light up Christmas tree. The list goes on and on. I really didn’t think we’d be affected too much. But when it got dark things got tougher & colder. Oh did I mention we had no car at home so me & Harper had to stick it out? I really felt like a little pioneer woman carrying around my lantern in the dark 😂 I take for granted these things I use every day. Like my light switch & washing machine. I’m extra grateful for them today 💕 Look around & thank God for something that you haven’t in a while. Like your health. Your safe family. Your clean running water. Being able to kiss your babies. Warm blankets. There is soo much to thank Him for.

Then he laughed so hard as he jumped down into the foam and, of course, he wanted to do it again. I told him to wait his turn as anothrr kid was at the top.

His turn came aroubd and as he got close to the top, another little boy, not much older than him sped past him and said "I got there first" in a tobe of voice that made my son feel really bad about himself. He gave me a look like he was about to cry. It was very upsetting. I looked around for that boy's parents. 
I continued to watch him after he left the tower and saw that his mom was sitting in a group talking to other moms. She wasnt watching where he was. I simply do not understand this. I am always watching my kid and if he wanders away, I will stop mid-sentence and follow him.

Unfortunately, this is something I see all the time. Parents not paying attention and therefore not correcting behavior and telling their children to take turns. I have even witnessed crying children on the playground and have had to go find their parents!

I have taught my son to take turns and play nicely, as a result, he often ends up bullied by these unsupervised children. It's frustrating to me as a parent who is trying to raise a respectful human being.
